articles.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a prisoner exchange as talks end with no big breakthrough
articles.dek: ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war, both sides said Wednesday as two days of U.S. mediated talks concluded with no major…

paragraphs.en: ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war, both sides said Wednesday as two days of U.S. mediated talks concluded with no major breakthrough on ending Moscow's nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion.
paragraphs.zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国阿布扎比——俄罗斯和乌克兰周三表示，双方已同意大规模交换战俘。为期两天的美国斡旋谈判结束，但未在结束莫斯科近5年全面入侵的问题上取得重大突破。

paragraphs.en: Hopes had been low for any significant development in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations. Russia and Ukraine have from time to time swapped POWs but have remained far apart in their demands for accepting a peace settlement.
paragraphs.zh: 对于两国代表团九个月来的首次会晤能取得任何重大进展，人们的期望一直很低。俄罗斯和乌克兰不时交换战俘，但在接受和平解决的要求上仍存在很大分歧。

paragraphs.en: U.S. officials say they are determined to revive Washington's peace efforts that so far have failed to deliver significant results.
paragraphs.zh: 美国官员表示，他们决心重振华盛顿的和平努力，而这些努力迄今为止未能取得显著成效。

paragraphs.en: Along with postwar security guarantees for both countries, other key hurdles are the fate of Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory and what role European countries will play in an eventual settlement.
paragraphs.zh: 除了为两国提供战后安全保障外，其他关键障碍还包括俄罗斯占领的乌克兰领土的命运，以及欧洲国家将在最终的解决方案中扮演何种角色。

paragraphs.en: The session was the first such meeting since February on Russia's invasion, which analysts and humanitarian organizations say has killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians.
paragraphs.zh: 这是自2月俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来的首次此类会议，分析人士和人道主义组织称，这场战争已造成数十万名士兵和数千名平民丧生。

paragraphs.en: The talks lasted just under two hours Wednesday, after a four-hour session the previous day.
paragraphs.zh: 在前一天进行四个小时的会谈后，周三的会谈持续了不到两个小时。

paragraphs.en: "One of the positives is we agreed that we're going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, which we're going to finalize the numbers tomorrow," said Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, after the Abu Dhabi talks ended.
paragraphs.zh: “其中一个积极因素是我们已经同意将进行最大规模的人道主义释放囚犯，我们将在明天敲定具体人数，”美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的女婿贾里德·库什纳在阿布扎比会谈结束后表示。

paragraphs.en: Vladimir Medinsky, head of the Russian delegation, and Rustem Umerov, who led Kyiv's contingent, confirmed the planned POW exchange, although Medinsky noted the agreement was "in principle."
paragraphs.zh: 俄罗斯代表团负责人弗拉基米尔·梅丁斯基以及基辅代表团负责人鲁斯特姆·乌梅罗夫确认了计划中的战俘交换，尽管梅丁斯基指出该协议是“原则性”的。

articles.title: Why is gasoline suddenly under $4 a gallon?
articles.dek: Drivers are starting to see some relief from high fuel prices. For the first time in months, the average price of a gallon of gasoline has dipped below $4, according to AAA.

paragraphs.en: Drivers are starting to see some relief from high fuel prices. For the first time in months, the average price of a gallon of gasoline has dipped below $4, according to AAA.
paragraphs.zh: 司机们开始从高油价中看到一些缓解。根据美国汽车协会（AAA）的数据，几个月来，汽油平均价格首次降至每加仑4美元以下。

paragraphs.en: The price crossed below the $4 threshold on Tuesday, and is currently down to a national average of $3.94 for a gallon of regular. Prices have dipped about 40 cents over the past month, with much of that decline happening in the past two weeks.
paragraphs.zh: 周二价格跌破了4美元的门槛，目前普通汽油的全国平均价格降至每加仑3.94美元。过去一个月价格已下跌约40美分，其中大部分下跌发生在过去两周。

paragraphs.en: Instead, he continued, gasoline prices are dropping for a more banal reason: "For now, it's the seasonal shift, not politics, driving the relief at the pump."
paragraphs.zh: 他接着说，汽油价格下跌的原因更为平凡：“目前，是季节性变化，而不是政治因素，推动了加油站价格的下降。”

paragraphs.en: One reason: It's no longer summer, which is the peak season for gas. (Fewer people drive in colder weather, AAA points out.) With less demand, there's a touch more gas on the market.
paragraphs.zh: 一个原因是：现在不再是夏天，而夏天是汽油的旺季。（AAA指出，天气冷的时候开车的人少。）需求减少，市场上的汽油供应稍微多一点。

paragraphs.en: Refineries also finish their annual maintenance by late fall. So that adds a bit more gas to go around.
paragraphs.zh: 炼油厂也会在晚秋之前完成年度维护。因此，这会增加一些可供应的汽油。

paragraphs.en: And the blend of gasoline that's on the market gets cheaper.
paragraphs.zh: 市面上的汽油混合物变得更便宜。

paragraphs.en: Refineries make two types of gasoline every year: summer and winter blends. The summer blend produces less smog, because it evaporates less quickly in the heat; the winter blend helps engines start up in freezing weather, and uses a bit more butane, which helps lower its cost.
paragraphs.zh: 炼油厂每年生产两种类型的汽油：夏季汽油和冬季汽油。夏季汽油产生的烟雾较少，因为它在高温下蒸发得较慢；冬季汽油有助于发动机在冰冻天气启动，并使用更多一些丁烷，这有助于降低其成本。

paragraphs.en: (Normally, the switch happens around September 15. This year, the Environmental Protection Agency and the Department of Energy said the switch would happen on September 1, citing gasoline prices that have been driven up by the war in Iran.)
paragraphs.zh: （通常，转换大约在9月15日发生。今年，环境保护局和能源部表示，由于伊朗战争导致汽油价格上涨，转换将于9月1日进行。）

paragraphs.en: But none of those are the biggest reason why gas prices are falling, says Jorge León, head of geopolitics at the research group Rystad Energy. The main driver is the falling price of Brent crude oil, which is now down to about $90 a barrel, and which is what refineries need to make gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，这些都不是油价下跌的最大原因，研究机构Rystad Energy地缘政治负责人Jorge León说。主要原因是布伦特原油价格下跌，现在已经降至大约每桶90美元，而炼油厂需要这种原油来生产汽油、柴油和喷气燃料。

articles.title: Investigation continues into Nvidia CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy
articles.dek: Fallout continues at the chip giant Nvidia. Its powerful CEO is accused of having an affair with a Chinese spy.

paragraphs.en: Fallout continues at the chip giant Nvidia. Its powerful CEO is accused of having an affair with a Chinese spy.
paragraphs.zh: 芯片巨头英伟达的动荡仍在继续。其强势的首席执行官被指控与一名中国间谍有染。

paragraphs.en: News that the AI chipmaker Nvidia is investigating its own CEO is reverberating from Wall Street to Capitol Hill.
paragraphs.zh: 关于人工智能芯片制造商英伟达正在调查其自身首席执行官的消息，从华尔街传到了国会山。

paragraphs.en: The company's stock slipped yesterday after the CEO, Jensen Huang, admitted to having an affair. News reports say it was with a woman that U.S. intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China.
paragraphs.zh: 在首席执行官黄仁勋承认有婚外情后，公司股票昨日下跌。新闻报道称，这名女性被美国情报机构怀疑为中国从事情报活动。

paragraphs.en: FADEL: NPR tech correspondent John Ruwitch joins us now to talk about this. Hey, John.
paragraphs.zh: FADEL：NPR 技术记者约翰·鲁维奇现在加入我们，来谈谈这个话题。嗨，约翰。

paragraphs.en: FADEL: Good morning. So just how bad has the fallout been so far for Nvidia?
paragraphs.zh: FADEL：早上好。那么到目前为止，英伟达的影响有多严重？

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: Yeah, it's not great. Nvidia's share price dropped around 4.25% yesterday. Meanwhile, Nvidia's main competitor in AI chips - the No. 2 player, AMD - leapt more than 13% on the news. Three committees in the House of Representatives have summoned Jensen Huang to a joint closed-door session next week to answer questions about the allegations. You know, Nvidia has a huge market share in the chips that are used to build and run AI. But a question that, you know, investors are starting to think they may have to grapple with is, if this snowballs, what does Nvidia look like without Jensen Huang at the helm? I mean, he cofounded the company and put it on the map.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：是的，这情况不太好。英伟达的股价昨天下跌了约4.25%。与此同时，英伟达在人工智能芯片领域的主要竞争对手——第二大厂商AMD——因这一消息股价飙升了超过13%。众议院三个委员会已召集黄仁勋下周参加联合闭门会议，回答有关指控的问题。你知道，英伟达在用于构建和运行人工智能的芯片中占有巨大市场份额。但一个问题是，投资者开始考虑，如果事态进一步扩大，没有黄仁勋领导的英伟达会是什么样子？我的意思是，他共同创办了公司，并让公司声名鹊起。

articles.title: World's fastest ocean liner is sunk to break another record: largest artificial reef
articles.dek: The fastest passenger liner in the world crossed the Atlantic Ocean in less than four days. On Wednesday, it sank in five hours.

paragraphs.en: The fastest passenger liner in the world crossed the Atlantic Ocean in less than four days. On Wednesday, it sank in five hours.
paragraphs.zh: 世界上最快的客轮在不到四天的时间内横渡了大西洋。星期三，它在五小时内沉没了。

paragraphs.en: The SS United States, launched in 1951 and longer than the RMS Titanic, once transported four presidents, the Mona Lisa and a slate of 20th century movie stars. After decades spent rusting, and facing the scrap heap, its minders settled on a deal to turn the vessel into what's expected to be the world's largest artificial reef off the coast of Okaloosa County, Fla.
paragraphs.zh: 美国联合号（SS United States）于1951年下水，其长度超过泰坦尼克号（RMS Titanic），曾运送过四位总统、《蒙娜丽莎》画作以及20世纪的一批电影明星。经过数十年生锈并面临报废，其管理者最终达成协议，将该船改造成预计将成为佛罗里达奥卡卢萨县海岸最大的人工珊瑚礁。

paragraphs.en: Crews removed plugs in the ship's hull, allowing it to fill with water without the use of explosives. After hours of delays, its final moments went quickly. The ship tilted onto its side and dipped below the waves.
paragraphs.zh: 船员们拆除了船体上的塞子，使船在不用炸药的情况下充满水。在几个小时的延误后，它的最后时刻很快到来。船倾斜到一侧，沉入波浪之下。

paragraphs.en: The sinking marks a bittersweet coda to the era of gleaming behemoths that crossed the seas in elegant fashion. It is also the latest in an ongoing effort by coastal communities to lure thrill-seeking tourists away from international destinations, one that has so far generated surprising economic benefits.
paragraphs.zh: 这次沉没标志着一个光辉庞然大物横渡大海、优雅航行时代的苦乐参半的尾声。这也是沿海社区为了吸引寻求刺激的游客远离国际目的地而进行的持续努力中的最新举措，到目前为止，这一努力已产生了令人惊讶的经济效益。

paragraphs.en: "For those of us who love shipwrecks and love ships in general, it was way more tragic to see it sitting and rusting away at the dock," wreck diver and maritime enthusiast Karen Flynn told NPR.
paragraphs.zh: 沉船潜水员和海事爱好者凯伦·弗林告诉NPR：“对于我们这些喜欢沉船并且总体上喜欢船的人来说，看着它停在码头上生锈、慢慢腐蚀是非常悲惨的。”

paragraphs.en: Her diving club, the Maryland-based Atlantic Wreck Divers, booked tickets and a charter boat just days after a date for the ship's "deployment," as the sinking is diplomatically described, was set.
paragraphs.zh: 她的潜水俱乐部——总部位于马里兰的亚特兰大残骸潜水员俱乐部——在沉船的“部署”（这是外交上对沉没的描述）日期确定的几天后，就预订了机票和包船。

paragraphs.en: "We've dove everything that you can around the world," Flynn said. "This will just be one more unique, new thing for us to dive."
paragraphs.zh: “我们已经潜过世界上所有可以潜的地方了，”弗林说。“这对我们来说只会是另一件独特的新潜水体验。”

paragraphs.en: In many ways, Flynn and her club are the exact type of visitor that Okaloosa County is hoping to attract: divers planning to stay overnight who will spend a fair amount of money on equipment, food and lodging during their travels.
paragraphs.zh: 在许多方面，弗林和她的俱乐部正是奥卡卢萨县希望吸引的那类游客：计划过夜的潜水者，他们在旅行中会在装备、食物和住宿上花费相当多的钱。

articles.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
articles.dek: One of America's most prominent political dynasties has waded into the growing fight against President Trump's proposed arch in Washington, D.C.

paragraphs.en: One of America's most prominent political dynasties has waded into the growing fight against President Trump's proposed arch in Washington, D.C.
paragraphs.zh: 美国最著名的政治世家之一已介入对特朗普总统拟建的华盛顿特区拱门的日益激烈的反对之中。

paragraphs.en: Nine members of the Kennedy family filed suit in federal court on Tuesday to block the 250-foot structure, saying it would obstruct their relatives' gravesites — including the John F. Kennedy Eternal Flame — at nearby Arlington National Cemetery.
paragraphs.zh: 肯尼迪家族的九名成员周二在联邦法院提起诉讼，试图阻止这座250英尺的建筑，称它将阻碍他们亲人的墓地，包括位于附近阿灵顿国家公墓的约翰·F·肯尼迪永恒之火。

paragraphs.en: "A towering arch casting shadows across the graves of our father, mother, and uncles, as well as the graves of so many who have served our country, would also cast a shadow over our democratic principles, undermining the safeguards established by our elected representatives to protect this hallowed ground for generations to come," Rory Kennedy and Maxwell Kennedy said in a statement on behalf of the family.
paragraphs.zh: 罗里·肯尼迪和麦克斯韦·肯尼迪代表家族在一份声明中表示：“一座高耸的拱门投下的阴影覆盖了我们父亲、母亲和叔叔的墓地，以及许多为国家服务者的墓地，也将对我们的民主原则投下阴影，削弱我们民选代表为保护这片神圣土地世代而建立的保障措施。”

paragraphs.en: The plaintiffs include children of Sen. Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy and a son of Sen. Edward M. Kennedy, all three of whom are buried at Arlington National Cemetery. There is one noticeable absence: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., did not join his siblings in the lawsuit against his own administration.
paragraphs.zh: 原告包括参议员罗伯特·F·肯尼迪和埃塞尔·肯尼迪的孩子，以及参议员爱德华·M·肯尼迪的一个儿子，这三人都安葬在阿灵顿国家公墓。有一个显著的缺席者：卫生与公共服务部部长罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 Jr.，没有加入控告自己政府的兄弟姐妹们的诉讼。

paragraphs.en: "It is unfortunate to see that some members of the Kennedy family have joined the litigation against the Arch as the project is intended to honor our heroes who rest in Arlington Cemetery," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told NPR in a statement. "We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds."
paragraphs.zh: 白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔在向NPR发表的一份声明中表示：“令人遗憾的是，肯尼迪家族的一些成员加入了针对拱门的诉讼，而该项目旨在纪念安息在阿灵顿公墓的英雄们。我们将继续为这一美丽而适宜的纪念碑辩护，并且有信心在诉讼过程中获得完全的平反。”

paragraphs.en: Max Kennedy, one of RFK's sons, told NPR's All Things Considered on Wednesday that his family is acting to protect Arlington National Cemetery from "the arbitrary, capricious vanity of one man."
paragraphs.zh: RFK的一个儿子马克斯·肯尼迪周三在NPR的《全面考虑》中表示，他的家人正在采取行动保护阿灵顿国家公墓，以防“一个人的任意、反复无常的虚荣”。

paragraphs.en: "This is one man who wants to build this arch," he said. "He's violated every rule. If this is a great idea, then bring it before Congress, follow the rules and get it approved."
paragraphs.zh: “这是一个想建造这座拱门的人，”他说。“他违反了所有的规则。如果这是一个好主意，那么就把它提交给国会，遵循规则并获得批准。”

paragraphs.en: The Kennedys' motion, filed hours before Veterans' Day, adds a highly personal layer to the ongoing legal fight.
paragraphs.zh: 肯尼迪家族在退伍军人节前几个小时提交的动议，为持续的法律斗争增添了高度个人化的层面。

articles.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running
articles.dek: GENEVA, Switzerland — The United States has left an empty chair at a key United Nations human rights review for the second year running, becoming the only U.N. member state ever to do so.

paragraphs.en: GENEVA, Switzerland — The United States has left an empty chair at a key United Nations human rights review for the second year running, becoming the only U.N. member state ever to do so.
paragraphs.zh: 瑞士日内瓦——美国连续第二年在联合国一项关键的人权审查会上留下空位，成为迄今唯一这样做的联合国会员国。

paragraphs.en: The review, known as the universal periodic review, is meant to be just that: universal. Each state is reviewed every four to five years by fellow member states. The aim is to ensure that every country, however powerful, undergoes a peer review of its human rights record.
paragraphs.zh: 这一审查，被称为普遍定期审查，正是意在如此：普遍。每个国家每四到五年由其他成员国进行一次审查。其目的是确保每个国家，无论多么强大，都要接受同侪对其人权记录的审查。

paragraphs.en: As well as diplomats from countries under review, civil society groups are allowed to submit evidence too. Several made the trip to Geneva, led by the American Civil Liberties Union.
paragraphs.zh: 除了受审查国家的外交官之外，民间社会团体也被允许提交证据。数个团体在美国公民自由联盟的带领下来到日内瓦。

paragraphs.en: Jamil Dakwar, the ACLU's human rights director, told journalists that the current U.S. administration was continuing to violate human rights "unabashed," citing the treatment of immigrants, student protesters and the LGBTQ community as examples.
paragraphs.zh: 美国公民自由联盟的人权主任贾米尔·达克瓦尔告诉记者，目前的美国政府“毫不掩饰”地继续侵犯人权，并以移民、学生抗议者和 LGBTQ 社群的待遇为例。

paragraphs.en: Dakwar said the U.N. must hold the U.S. accountable, warning that the Trump administration wanted to "dismantle human rights." In a written response, the State Department pointed out that Washington had already formally withdrawn from the U.N. Human Rights Council, accusing it of "pushing anti-American rhetoric."
paragraphs.zh: 达克瓦尔表示，联合国必须追究美国的责任，并警告说特朗普政府想要“拆除人权”。在书面回应中，国务院指出，华盛顿已经正式退出了联合国人权理事会，指责该理事会“推动反美言论”。

paragraphs.en: In fact, leaving the council, which has 47 elected members, does not mean the U.S. can easily get out of the review process, which is obligatory for all 193 U.N. member states. Human rights groups see Washington's stance as part of a pattern of disengagement and even active opposition to multilateral organizations, pointing to U.S. sanctions on the International Criminal Court and the decision to leave the World Health Organization.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，离开拥有47名民选成员的理事会，并不意味着美国可以轻易摆脱这一对所有193个联合国会员国都强制性的审查程序。人权组织认为，华盛顿的立场是脱离甚至积极反对多边组织的一种模式，他们指出美国对国际刑事法院的制裁以及决定退出世界卫生组织。

paragraphs.en: So what happens now? The U.N. has few sanctions against a country that does not cooperate with the review process. Israel skipped one review back in 2013 in protest at what it said was anti-Israel bias, but returned nine months later after the U.N. rescheduled. Until today's no-show by the U.S., no country has ever failed to turn up twice.
paragraphs.zh: 那么现在会发生什么？联合国对不配合审查程序的国家几乎没有制裁。以色列在2013年因为抗议其所谓的反以色列偏见而错过了一次审查，但在联合国重新安排后九个月又回来了。在今天美国未出席之前，还没有任何国家曾经两次缺席。

paragraphs.en: Rights groups would like the U.N. to hold the review anyway, and take evidence about alleged violations in the U.S. Member states had already drawn up a list of questions for Washington's diplomats, including questions about the use of the death penalty and restrictions on abortion.
paragraphs.zh: 人权组织希望联合国无论如何都进行审查，并收集有关美国涉嫌侵权的证据。成员国已经为华盛顿的外交官拟定了一份问题清单，包括关于死刑使用和堕胎限制的问题。

articles.title: The scandal surrounding the head of Nvidia could have wide-ranging implications
articles.dek: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Bloomberg tech reporter Ian King about the unusually overarching role of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at his company and within the American tech industry at large.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Bloomberg tech reporter Ian King about the unusually overarching role of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at his company and within the American tech industry at large.
paragraphs.zh: NPR 的 Sacha Pfeiffer 与彭博科技记者 Ian King 谈论了英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在公司以及整个美国科技行业中异常广泛的角色。

paragraphs.en: He is the CEO of an American tech giant. She was a Chinese executive at a firm in Singapore. And their liaison could cost him everything. That sounds like a soap opera, and yet it is a thing that has actually happened to Jensen Huang, whose company, NVIDIA, creates many of the world's most powerful computer chips. U.S. intelligence agencies believe the Chinese businesswoman was actually a spy for China. China denies that. But on Sunday, Jensen Huang did admit to the affair, and NVIDIA has lost hundreds of billions of dollars in market value in the last two days. How important is Jensen Huang to NVIDIA, and how important is NVIDIA to the U.S. economy? Those are two of the questions I'm going to put to Ian King. He's been writing about this story for Bloomberg. Ian, welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 他是一家美国科技巨头的首席执行官。她曾是新加坡一家公司的中国高管。他们之间的关系可能会让他失去一切。这听起来像一部肥皂剧，但这实际上发生在黄仁勋身上，他的公司英伟达制造了世界上许多最强大的计算机芯片。美国情报机构认为，这位中国女商人实际上是为中国进行间谍活动的人。中国对此予以否认。但在周日，黄仁勋确实承认了这段关系，而英伟达在过去两天内市值蒸发了数千亿美元。黄仁勋对英伟达有多重要，而英伟达对美国经济有多重要？这些是我要问布隆伯格记者伊恩·金的两个问题。伊恩，一直在报道这个故事。欢迎你，伊恩。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: Ian, anyone who follows the stock market knows that a company like NVIDIA has been underpinning the U.S. economy enormously through its dominant role in U.S. financial markets. Tell us why that matters when we talk about this what otherwise might be a sort of simple corporate affair scandal story.
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：Ian，任何关注股市的人都知道，像英伟达这样的公司通过其在美国金融市场中的主导地位极大地支撑了美国经济。告诉我们，当我们谈论这一可能本来只是一个简单的企业丑闻故事时，这为什么很重要。

paragraphs.en: KING: No, that's exactly the right question. Jensen Huang is the only CEO that NVIDIA has ever had. He is absolutely central to how it acts, its strategy and everything else, that he has a unique corporate structure (ph). If it was only that, that would be of note to NVIDIA investors, and there are a lot of them. But even more than that, he has been the cheerleader for the U.S.'s efforts to promote artificial intelligence and to try to propagate that industry throughout the world. And in addition to that, he has pledged literally tens of billions of dollars in investments to fund other companies' efforts to get up to speed and to move that all forward.
paragraphs.zh: KING：不，这正是正确的问题。黄仁勋是英伟达有史以来唯一的首席执行官。他对公司的运作、战略及其他所有方面都至关重要，以至于他拥有独特的公司结构。如果仅仅是这样，这对英伟达的投资者来说已经值得关注，而且投资者有很多。但更重要的是，他一直是美国推动人工智能发展并试图在全球推广这一产业的积极支持者。除此之外，他还承诺投入数百亿美元的投资，以资助其他公司加速发展并推动这一切前进。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: Do you consider him a different type of CEO than other tech CEOs? Is he distinctive in some way?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：你认为他与其他科技公司的首席执行官是不同类型的吗？他在某些方面有独特之处吗？

paragraphs.en: KING: He's distinctive in many ways. The most important thing is that this company was built around him. His staff are absolutely devoted to him. They can't answer questions without referring to what he says. He sits in a room. His office isn't an office. It's essentially a small auditorium where the people that report to him sit and face his scrutiny. He can be very harsh. He can also be very supportive. He never fires people. He deals with customers. He deals with the government relations. The front man, he's the head - he's everything and consciously so for this company.
paragraphs.zh: KING：他在许多方面都很独特。最重要的是，这家公司是围绕他建立的。他的员工对他绝对忠诚。他们在回答问题时都必须参考他的话。他坐在一个房间里。他的办公室不是真正的办公室，它本质上是一个小型礼堂，向他汇报的人坐在那里，接受他的审查。他可能非常严格，也可能非常支持。他从不解雇人。他处理客户关系，也处理政府事务。作为门面，他是负责人——他是公司的一切，而且公司对此心知肚明。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: He's the opposite of a hands-off manager. He's down there on the floor with the worker bees. He kind of gets all aspects of the company?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：他完全不是那种放手不管的管理者。他就在一线和工蜂们在一起。他有点了解公司的各个方面，对吗？

paragraphs.en: KING: He acts like he owns it, and the people who work for him act like he owns the company. That's the bottom line, despite the fact that that's not true, despite the fact that it's a $4 trillion company. He hasn't got anything in the way of a succession plan that would lead you to believe, well, OK, maybe in the case of Microsoft, when Bill Gates leaves, Steve Ballmer steps up and everything's OK. That's just not the way NVIDIA is run and the way NVIDIA is structured.
paragraphs.zh: 国王：他表现得好像自己拥有它，而为他工作的人也表现得好像他拥有这家公司。这就是根本问题，尽管事实并非如此，尽管这是一家市值4万亿美元的公司。他没有任何继任计划，让你觉得，嗯，好吧，也许在微软的情况下，当比尔·盖茨离开时，史蒂夫·鲍默会接任，一切都会没问题。但NVIDIA并不是这样运作和组织的。

articles.title: Testing the new generation of AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones
articles.dek: On a rare overcast day in late summer, red-and-white fire trucks pepper a grassy strip of land in the mountains of western Colorado.

paragraphs.en: On a rare overcast day in late summer, red-and-white fire trucks pepper a grassy strip of land in the mountains of western Colorado.
paragraphs.zh: 在夏末一个罕见的阴天，红白相间的消防车点缀在科罗拉多西部山区的一片草地上。

paragraphs.en: A persistent buzzing rises and falls as several uniformed staff from the Aspen Fire Protection District huddle around an iPad, watching one of their volunteer firefighters control a massive drone.
paragraphs.zh: 当来自阿斯彭消防保护区的几名穿制服的工作人员围在一台iPad周围，观看他们的一名志愿消防员操控一台巨大的无人机时，一种持续的嗡嗡声时高时低地响起。

paragraphs.en: This first-of-its-kind machine looks like a giant bug. Black and white with propellers attached to four large arms, it's about 10 by 12 feet wide — roughly the size of a small U-Haul trailer.
paragraphs.zh: 这款首创的机器看起来像一只巨大的虫子。它是黑白相间的，四个大臂上装有螺旋桨，宽约10乘12英尺——大约是一个小型U-Haul拖车的大小。

paragraphs.en: While firefighters have used drones to monitor wildfires for decades, this new product could use AI to help extinguish fires.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然消防员已经使用无人机监控野火几十年，但这款新产品可以利用人工智能帮助扑灭火灾。

paragraphs.en: Developed by the California-based company Seneca, the drones are designed to work in a swarm. Similar to a small fire engine, five of them can carry 500 to 1,000 gallons of finished fire foam, and firefighters in Aspen reported they were easy to operate.
paragraphs.zh: 由位于加利福尼亚的公司塞内卡开发，这些无人机被设计为群体协作。类似于一辆小型消防车，五架无人机可以携带500到1000加仑的成品灭火泡沫，阿斯本的消防员报告说它们操作起来很容易。

paragraphs.en: "We were just joking that my 12-year-old could fly these things," said Andy Fisher, deputy chief of Aspen Fire.
paragraphs.zh: 阿斯本消防副局长安迪·费舍尔说：“我们只是在开玩笑，说我12岁的孩子都能驾驶这些东西。”

paragraphs.en: When Aspen Fire officially launches its new drone program, as early as next year, it'll be the first fire department in the world to operate the drones independently. So far, they've only been used on prescribed burns in California with support from Seneca's staff.
paragraphs.zh: 当阿斯本消防局正式启动其新的无人机项目时，最早可能在明年，它将成为世界上第一个独立操作无人机的消防部门。到目前为止，它们仅在加州的规定烧除中使用，并且有塞内卡工作人员的支持。

paragraphs.en: Fisher wants to send these drones to hard-to-reach fires, like remote lightning strikes, before firefighters arrive. The city of Aspen, famously home to billions of dollars in real estate, is surrounded by dense forests — like an expensive tinderbox with few evacuation routes for residents and visitors.
paragraphs.zh: 费舍尔希望在消防员到达之前，将这些无人机送到难以到达的火灾现场，比如偏远的雷击地点。著名的阿斯彭市，以数十亿美元的房地产闻名，四周被浓密的森林包围——就像一个昂贵的火药桶，居民和游客的疏散路线很少。

articles.title: Climate change is altering the colors we see in the world: an illustrated journey
articles.dek: Imagine the bright tones of coral under the sea. What do you see? What colors come to mind?

paragraphs.en: Imagine the bright tones of coral under the sea. What do you see? What colors come to mind?
paragraphs.zh: 想象海底珊瑚的明亮色调。你看到了什么？脑海中浮现出哪些颜色？

paragraphs.en: One of the ways that climate change will alter — or has already altered — our world is by shifting the familiar colors of nature. When warming ocean waters bleach the vibrant colors of coral to white, that’s one example.
paragraphs.zh: 气候变化将改变——或已经改变——我们世界的一种方式是通过改变自然界熟悉的颜色。当变暖的海水将珊瑚鲜艳的颜色漂白成白色时，这就是一个例子。

paragraphs.en: “Many young scientists who are working on coral reefs don’t realize that what they’re seeing is vastly degraded,” says Anya Salih, a scientist who has studied coral reefs and their fluorescent colors for decades. “It’s often hard to perceive how it was to what it is now.”
paragraphs.zh: “许多从事珊瑚礁研究的年轻科学家并没有意识到他们所看到的其实已经严重退化，”长期研究珊瑚礁及其荧光色彩的科学家安雅·萨利赫说。“通常很难察觉它曾经的样子与现在的差距。”

paragraphs.en: This change of color isn’t just aesthetic. For coral, bleaching leaves them vulnerable to disease and other stressors that can lead to death. In other situations, these color changes have more complex impacts, ones that scientists are still trying to understand.
paragraphs.zh: 这种颜色的变化不仅仅是审美上的。对于珊瑚来说，白化会使它们容易受到疾病和其他压力因素的影响，这些都可能导致死亡。在其他情况下，这些颜色变化有更复杂的影响，科学家们仍在试图理解这些影响。

paragraphs.en: Every summer, massive climate-driven wildfires spread soot across huge swaths of the Arctic, covering the ice in a blanket of black particles. Soot pollution from oil and gas operations, as well as commercial shipping and increased tourism, contributes to the problem at both poles.
paragraphs.zh: 每年夏天，由气候驱动的大规模野火会将烟尘传播到北极的大片地区，为冰层覆盖上一层黑色颗粒的毯子。来自油气作业、商业航运以及增加的旅游活动的烟尘污染，也在两极加剧了这一问题。

paragraphs.en: The dark particles coat white snow and soak up heat from the sun, exacerbating melting that was already happening more quickly because of climate change. Increased melting in the Arctic leads to sea level rise, which threatens communities across the world. And the soot itself pollutes the air and water it seeps into.
paragraphs.zh: 黑色颗粒覆盖在白雪上并吸收太阳的热量，加剧了由于气候变化已经加快的融化。北极地区融化的增加导致海平面上升，这威胁着世界各地的社区。而黑碳本身也污染了其渗入的空气和水。

paragraphs.en: “We know that the high northern latitudes are warming faster than the rest of the planet,” says Douglas Morton, an Earth scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. These changes are shifting the colors of the Arctic landscape.
paragraphs.zh: “我们知道，高纬度地区的变暖速度比地球其他地区更快，”美国宇航局戈达德太空飞行中心的地球科学家道格拉斯·莫顿说。这些变化正在改变北极景观的颜色。

paragraphs.en: Annual surface air temperature, departure from the 1991-2020 mean
paragraphs.zh: 年度地表空气温度，相对于1991-2020年均值的偏差

paragraphs.en: Beyond the Arctic ice at the pole, farther south, lie vast regions of permafrost: soil that has remained frozen for years.
paragraphs.zh: 在北极冰层以外，更向南，是广阔的永久冻土区：多年保持冻结的土壤。

paragraphs.en: How much money would it take for you to feel financially secure? Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Mona Chalabi spent five years following 10 Americans, from those living paycheck to paycheck to those earning hundreds of thousands of dollars a year, in an effort to answer that question. Her new book, Ten Lives: How What We Have Shapes Who We Are, explores why financial security can feel so elusive.
paragraphs.zh: 需要多少钱才能让你感到财务安全？普利策奖获奖记者莫娜·查拉比花了五年时间跟踪调查了10名美国人，从靠工资勉强度日的人到年收入数十万美元的人，试图回答这个问题。她的新书《十种人生：我们拥有什么塑造了我们是谁》探讨了为什么财务安全感会显得如此难以捉摸。

paragraphs.en: "It's called 10 Lives because I specifically didn't just want to focus on the 1%," Chalabi says. "Instead I wanted to talk about how the 99% of us aren't all in it together, and the kind of power differentials between us."
paragraphs.zh: 查拉比说：“它被称为《10条生命》，因为我特别不想只关注1%。相反，我想谈谈我们99%的人并不是完全站在一起的，以及我们之间存在的权力差异。”

paragraphs.en: Chalabi says almost everyone she profiled in the book was deeply worried about their financial future, even those who earn plenty of money.
paragraphs.zh: 查拉比说，她在书中描写的几乎每个人都对自己的财务未来非常担忧，即使是那些赚很多钱的人也是如此。

paragraphs.en: "Across the board, everyone just seemed to be expressing this feeling of panic that I think is really, really particular to U.S. capitalism, which is an incredibly precarious and cruel system where you are one crisis away from experiencing a real economic shock," she says.
paragraphs.zh: “总体而言，每个人似乎都在表达这种恐慌的感觉，我认为这确实是美国资本主义特有的，这是一种极其不稳定和残酷的制度，你可能因为一次危机就遭遇真正的经济冲击，”她说。

paragraphs.en: Chalabi also noticed that many of the people she profiled considered themselves middle class, regardless of what their actual income was. She says that disconnect between actual wealth and a sense of class has consequences — not just for how we see ourselves, but also in how we judge everybody else.
paragraphs.zh: 查拉比还注意到，她所描绘的许多人认为自己是中产阶级，不管他们的实际收入是多少。她说，实际财富与阶级感之间的这种脱节有其后果——不仅影响我们如何看待自己，也影响我们如何评判其他人。

paragraphs.en: "To be poor in this country is to encounter an enormous, enormous array of obstacles, including assumptions about your intelligence [and] your educational level," she says. "And so it's actually quite rational sometimes for people to try to present themselves as middle class, maybe even to try and signal wealth with the clothes that they buy or the cars that they drive. I don't think it's simply aspirational. I also think it is them trying to avoid the discrimination that they might face if their real income level were disclosed."
paragraphs.zh: “在这个国家，贫穷意味着要面对大量、巨大的障碍，包括人们对你的智力和教育水平的假设，”她说。“因此，有时候人们试图表现得像中产阶级，甚至通过他们购买的衣服或驾驶的汽车来显示财富，实际上是相当理性的。我不认为这仅仅是追求向上；我也认为这是他们试图避免如果真实收入水平被公开可能面临的歧视。”

paragraphs.en: On the importance of parents when it comes to financial security
paragraphs.zh: 论父母在财务安全方面的重要性

paragraphs.en: If you really want to understand somebody's economic security, you need to understand who they can turn to when times get hard, and obviously a household is an imperfect measure of that. People sometimes even live with spouses that they can't necessarily lean on. ... But one of the things that came out time and time and time again from the book is how much money your parents have is so profound in shaping your economic security. …
paragraphs.zh: 如果你真的想了解某人的经济安全状况，你需要了解他们在困难时期可以依靠谁，而显然一个家庭是对此不完全准确的衡量标准。人们有时甚至会和他们不一定可以依靠的配偶生活在一起。……但这本书一次又一次强调的一点是，你父母有多少钱在塑造你的经济安全方面有着深远的影响。……

articles.title: France accuses Iran of cyber 'sabotage' in fridge attacks
articles.dek: France is accusing Iran of having launched a series of destructive cyberattacks against its critical infrastructure in October.

paragraphs.en: France is accusing Iran of having launched a series of destructive cyberattacks against its critical infrastructure in October.
paragraphs.zh: 法国指责伊朗在十月对其关键基础设施发动了一系列破坏性网络攻击。

paragraphs.en: According to the French National Cybersecurity Agency, ANSSI, Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 different retail sites in France, from supermarkets to butcher shops, turning up the temperature in the middle of the night and spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food.
paragraphs.zh: 根据法国国家网络安全局（ANSSI）的说法，伊朗军事黑客接管了法国大约700个不同零售场所的制冷控制器，从超市到肉店，在深夜调高温度，导致价值数百万美元的食品被毁坏。

paragraphs.en: They also targeted several small hydroelectric power plants, resulting in "moderate effects," wrote ANSSI in its press release.
paragraphs.zh: ANSSI在其新闻稿中写道，他们还针对了几座小型水电站，造成了“中等影响”。

paragraphs.en: The hacking campaign was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression," said French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot. He said it "marks the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people."
paragraphs.zh: 法国外交部长让-诺埃尔·巴罗表示，这次黑客行动在规模和攻击性水平上都是“前所未有的”。他表示，这“标志着首次针对我国国土进行的大规模破坏性网络攻击，并构成了对国家利益和法国人民安全的重大攻击。”

paragraphs.en: The Paris Prosecutor's Office has opened its own investigation into the Iranian cyber unit, Shahid Kaveh, which the French government is linking to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. "The Paris Public Prosecutor's Office is requesting the issuance of international arrest warrants," the office said in a statement.
paragraphs.zh: 巴黎检察官办公室已经对伊朗网络单位Shahid Kaveh展开了自己的调查，法国政府将其与伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队联系起来。检察官办公室在一份声明中表示：“巴黎公共检察官办公室正在请求发布国际逮捕令。”

paragraphs.en: The attacks on French industrial controllers are part of a larger trend. In 2026 alone, hackers have targeted refrigeration controllers from Europe to Israel and the United States.
paragraphs.zh: 对法国工业控制器的攻击是更大趋势的一部分。仅在2026年，黑客就已经针对从欧洲到以色列和美国的制冷控制器进行了攻击。

paragraphs.en: Grocery stores in European countries including Sweden and Ireland were hit in similar attacks last week.
paragraphs.zh: 包括瑞典和爱尔兰在内的欧洲国家的杂货店上周遭到了类似的袭击。

paragraphs.en: In a separate incident in France, employees at a major French blood bank had to act fast to save blood samples from heating up when their refrigeration system was hit last week, prompting international calls for the health sector to protect its lifesaving products from spoiling.
paragraphs.zh: 在法国的另一事件中，上周一家主要法国血液银行的员工在其制冷系统受损时不得不迅速行动，以防血液样本升温，这引发了国际上呼吁卫生部门保护其救命产品不被损坏。

paragraphs.en: In Israel in the spring, suspected Iranian hackers going by the name of "Cyber Isnaad Front" claimed responsibility for sabotaging an industrial food processing plant, including infecting its corporate computers with malware, taking over office printers to print out threatening messages and hacking office cameras for use in a propaganda video released in early October. That video included a taunt in French referencing ongoing education-related protests, and came just before the attacks on French supermarket fridges. Cyber incident response firm Profero attributed the Israel attack to a wing of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps.
paragraphs.zh: 在以色列的春季，自称为“网络援助前线”的疑似伊朗黑客声称负责破坏一家工业食品加工厂，包括用恶意软件感染其公司计算机、接管办公室打印机打印威胁信息以及入侵办公室摄像头，用于拍摄一则在十月初发布的宣传视频。该视频包含用法语的挑衅内容，提及正在进行的教育相关抗议活动，并且紧接在法国超市冰箱遭攻击之前。网络事件响应公司Profero将这次以色列的攻击归因于伊朗革命卫队的一个分支。

articles.title: Nvidia shares tumble as the company says it's investigating CEO Jensen Huang
articles.dek: Nvidia's share price falls after the company begins an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

paragraphs.en: Nvidia's share price falls after the company begins an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.
paragraphs.zh: 在公司开始调查首席执行官黄仁勋与一名被指控为中国间谍的女性的所谓关系后，英伟达的股价下跌。

paragraphs.en: Shares in the chipmaker NVIDIA tumbled today. That's because the $4.3 trillion company said it is investigating its CEO, and that is due to allegations that he had a relationship with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy. NPR tech correspondent John Ruwitch is here to bring us up to speed. Hi, John.
paragraphs.zh: 芯片制造商英伟达的股票今天暴跌。原因是，这家市值4.3万亿美元的公司表示正在调查其首席执行官，这是因为有指控称他与一名被美国情报部门怀疑为中国间谍的女性有关系。NPR科技记者约翰·鲁维奇在这里为我们带来最新情况。你好，约翰。

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: Yeah. Yesterday, NVIDIA posted two announcements online. One said the board was investigating CEO Jensen Huang after reports that he was, quote, "the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The other was a memo from Huang himself admitting to having an affair and saying that he'd cooperate with the investigation. Now, The New York Times and others have been reporting that U.S. intelligence agencies believe that Huang became involved with a Chinese woman at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed. That company was a customer buying NVIDIA chips.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：是的。昨天，英伟达在网上发布了两个公告。一个说董事会正在调查首席执行官黄仁勋，此前有报道称他是“外国情报活动的目标”。另一个是黄本人发出的备忘录，承认有婚外情，并表示将配合调查。现在，《纽约时报》和其他媒体报道称，美国情报机构认为，黄参与了与一家总部位于新加坡的公司Megaspeed的中国女性的关系。这家公司是购买英伟达芯片的客户。

paragraphs.en: Those reports, which NPR has not independently corroborated, said the woman was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Huang or possibly try to influence U.S. policy. The New York Times has reported that Megaspeed was being investigated by the government for circumventing U.S. export controls and helping Chinese tech companies get access to restricted chips. I reached out to Megaspeed and haven't heard back, but the company has previously denied wrongdoing.
paragraphs.zh: 这些报道称，该女子被中国国家安全部招募，以监视黄某，或可能试图影响美国政策，NPR 尚未独立证实这些报道。《纽约时报》报道称，Megaspeed 正在接受政府调查，因为其规避美国出口管制并帮助中国科技公司获取受限制的芯片。我联系了 Megaspeed，但尚未收到回复，不过该公司此前否认有任何不当行为。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: John, as you know, China spying on foreign companies is not uncommon. So explain why this one is so headline-grabbing.
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：约翰，你也知道，中国对外国公司的间谍活动并不罕见。那么解释一下，为什么这次会如此引人注意。

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: Yeah. I covered China for a number of years, and foreign businesses in China were constantly complaining about the government trying to hack or spy on them to learn their corporate secrets. But NVIDIA is really in a league of its own in terms of its importance. You know, the chips that NVIDIA makes are crucial to the AI boom. The company's also entangled in a web of investments with other AI companies. So for example, NVIDIA has invested in OpenAI and Anthropic, and in turn, those companies are buying chips from NVIDIA.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：是的。我曾报道过中国好几年，外国企业在中国经常抱怨政府试图入侵或监视他们，以了解他们的企业机密。但在重要性方面，NVIDIA 确实是独一无二的。你知道，NVIDIA 生产的芯片对人工智能的快速发展至关重要。该公司还与其他人工智能公司有着复杂的投资关系。例如，NVIDIA 投资了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，而这些公司反过来又从 NVIDIA 购买芯片。

paragraphs.en: NVIDIA and its chips are also right at the center of the AI competition between the U.S. and China. The U.S. banned NVIDIA's best chips from being sold there out of a concern that they could be used to help China's AI industry catch up with the U.S. But Jensen Huang, the CEO, has been one of the most prominent voices arguing against that ban. He says it would be actually good for the U.S. if Chinese companies were hooked on American chips.
paragraphs.zh: 英伟达及其芯片也正处于美中人工智能竞争的中心。美国出于担心这些芯片可能被用来帮助中国的人工智能产业追赶美国，而禁止在美销售英伟达最好的芯片。但首席执行官黄仁勋一直是反对这一禁令的最突出声音之一。他表示，如果中国公司依赖美国芯片，实际上对美国是有好处的。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: And the company now has to decide what to do about this and what to do about him, whether maybe to dismiss him. I mean, give us a sense of how important he is to this company.
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：公司现在必须决定如何处理这件事以及如何处理他，是否可能解雇他。我的意思是，让我们了解一下他对这家公司有多重要。

articles.title: Palantir hires a former Democratic senator as it faces scrutiny in new Congress
articles.dek: Tech companies are expecting a wave of scrutiny from Democrats for the industry's ties with the Trump administration when they take over Congress in January. In anticipation, many are hiring…

paragraphs.en: Tech companies are expecting a wave of scrutiny from Democrats for the industry's ties with the Trump administration when they take over Congress in January. In anticipation, many are hiring former Democratic lawmakers and aides to make their case to the incoming House and Senate majorities.
paragraphs.zh: 科技公司预计，当民主党在一月接管国会时，由于该行业与特朗普政府的联系，将面临民主党的审查浪潮。为了应对，许多公司正在雇佣前民主党议员和助手，以向即将上任的众议院和参议院多数派阐述他们的立场。

paragraphs.en: Among the latest to make that move is Palantir, which has hired former Sen. Jon Tester, a colorful Montana Democrat who's also an organic farmer.
paragraphs.zh: 最近采取这一举动的公司之一是Palantir，该公司聘请了前参议员乔恩·特斯特，他是蒙大拿州的一个多彩的民主党人，同时也是一名有机农民。

paragraphs.en: "My agreement with Palantir is advisory in nature, it is not lobbying," Tester, who lost reelection to the Senate in 2024, told NPR in an interview.
paragraphs.zh: 在接受NPR采访时，2024年失去参议院连任的特斯特表示：“我与Palantir的协议是咨询性质的，不是游说。”

paragraphs.en: The secretive American software and artificial intelligence company has drawn the ire of Democrats in Congress during President Trump's second term. Palantir — named by billionaire founder Peter Theil after the mythical "seeing stone" from J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings — has been accused of abetting mass surveillance on Americans and immigrants.
paragraphs.zh: 这家神秘的美国软件和人工智能公司在特朗普总统任期的第二阶段引起了国会中民主党的愤怒。Palantir——由亿万富翁创始人彼得·蒂尔以J.R.R. 托尔金《指环王》中的神话“洞察石”命名——被指控助长对美国人和移民的全面监控。

paragraphs.en: "Perception is reality in Washington, D.C. and in politics in general," said Tester. "But the fact is, I think Palantir has got a good story to tell, and they need to tell it. And hopefully folks will be receptive to it."
paragraphs.zh: 特斯特说：“在华盛顿特区以及整体政治中，感知就是现实。但事实上，我认为Palantir有一个很好的故事要讲，而且他们需要讲出来。希望人们能够接受。”

paragraphs.en: Palantir has long denied claims it aids mass surveillance on the American public — saying it doesn't gather or manipulate data at all, but instead creates tools for government agencies and private companies to organize and optimize their own information. The company has said it is committed to "protecting privacy and upholding liberal democratic values."
paragraphs.zh: Palantir 长期以来一直否认其协助对美国公众进行大规模监控的说法——称其根本不收集或操纵数据，而是为政府机构和私人公司创建工具，以组织和优化它们自己的信息。该公司表示，它致力于“保护隐私并维护自由民主价值观。”

paragraphs.en: Earlier this year, while in the minority, Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., along with 30 other Democratic lawmakers demanded answers about Palantir's contracts with the Department of Homeland Security and whether its tools are part of efforts by the federal government to surveil Americans. Palantir denied the accusation and said it is "neither conducting nor enabling mass surveillance of American citizens," but Wyden wasn't fully satisfied with its response, according to his Senate office.
paragraphs.zh: 今年早些时候，当时身处少数派的俄勒冈州民主党参议员罗恩·怀登（Sen. Ron Wyden）与其他30位民主党议员一起，要求就Palantir与国土安全部的合同提供答案，并询问其工具是否是联邦政府监视美国人的努力的一部分。Palantir否认了这一指控，并表示其“既不进行也不支持对美国公民的大规模监控”，但据怀登的参议院办公室称，他对其回应并不完全满意。

paragraphs.en: "Senator Wyden has a number of questions about Palantir's work to facilitate the Trump-Vance abuse of government data that he intends to ask again as chairman of the Finance Committee," Wyden's staff wrote in a statement to NPR. "If Palantir is not responsive next year, compulsory processes will be on the table."

articles.title: Trump administration moves to lift ban on roadbuilding and logging in national forests
articles.dek: The Trump administration is working to rescind the "Roadless Rule," which blocks road construction in some national forests. This could affect Alaska's Tongass National Forest.

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration is working to rescind the "Roadless Rule," which blocks road construction in some national forests. This could affect Alaska's Tongass National Forest.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府正在努力废除“无路规则”，该规则禁止在一些国家森林中修建道路。这可能会影响阿拉斯加的汤加斯国家森林。

paragraphs.en: For decades, an administrative rule known as the Roadless Rule banned new road building and logging across millions of acres of national forest lands. Now the Trump administration has moved to lift the ban. That's controversial in places like Alaska's Tongass National Forest, the largest national forest in the U.S. Reporter Alix Soliman from member station KTOO has the story.
paragraphs.zh: 几十年来，一项被称为“无路规则”的行政规定禁止在数百万英亩的国家森林土地上新建道路和采伐木材。如今，特朗普政府已采取行动取消这一禁令。这在阿拉斯加的通加斯国家森林等地引发了争议，该森林是美国最大的国家森林。会员电台KTOO的记者Alix Soliman带来了报道。

paragraphs.en: ALIX SOLIMAN, BYLINE: Around half of the Tongass National Forest in Southeast Alaska has no active roads. That's more than 9 million acres.
paragraphs.zh: 阿利克斯·索利曼，署名：阿拉斯加东南部的通加斯国家森林约有一半没有通行道路。这超过 900 万英亩。

paragraphs.en: SOLIMAN: On a recent afternoon, Judith Daxootsu Ramos walked through a roadless area. She's a Tlingit anthropologist from Yakutat, a small Alaska Native village. And she says the forest supports a number of Tlingit traditions, like harvesting berries and hunting deer.
paragraphs.zh: SOLIMAN：在一个最近的下午，朱迪斯·达克苏图·拉莫斯走过一片没有道路的地区。她是来自雅库塔特，一个阿拉斯加原住民小村庄的特林吉特人类学家。她说，这片森林支持许多特林吉特人的传统活动，比如采摘浆果和打猎鹿。

paragraphs.en: JUDITH DAXOOTSU RAMOS: Without this, we're going to lose our traditional medicines, our traditional art styles, our traditional foods. And all of that is really connected to the forest.
paragraphs.zh: 朱迪思·达克舒特苏·拉莫斯：没有这些，我们将失去我们的传统药物、传统艺术风格、传统食物。而这一切都与森林密切相关。

paragraphs.en: SOLIMAN: Ramos sits on the board of the Southeast Alaska Conservation Council, a local nonprofit advocating to keep the Roadless Rule in place. She visited Prince of Wales Island, a heavily logged part of the forest, and says the trees that grew back in old-growth clearcuts looked sterile.
paragraphs.zh: SOLIMAN：拉莫斯是东南阿拉斯加保护委员会的董事会成员，该委员会是一个本地非营利组织，倡导维持无道路区规则。她访问了威尔士亲王岛，这是森林中被大量伐木的地区，她表示在老林区清伐后重新生长的树木看起来毫无生气。

paragraphs.en: RAMOS: It's a very different forest. And there was no animals, no birds there, and it was kind of really quiet. And so it was kind of scary.
paragraphs.zh: 拉莫斯：这是一个完全不同的森林。那里没有动物，没有鸟，而且非常安静。所以有点可怕。

paragraphs.en: SOLIMAN: Others in the region oppose lifting the Roadless Rule because they worry it will hurt ecotourism or undermine the climate benefits of the Tongass, which holds a third of all carbon stored in intact U.S. national forests. But the U.S. Department of Agriculture says that it wants to roll back the Roadless Rule to give firefighters access to fight wildfires and remove what they say are outdated regulatory barriers. But many in this part of Alaska think it's to increase logging. The Trump administration has tried to boost national timber production in the past, and the first Trump administration temporarily rolled back the rule in just the Tongass.
paragraphs.zh: SOLIMAN：该地区的其他人反对取消无路区规则，因为他们担心这会损害生态旅游或削弱汤加斯国家森林的气候效益，而汤加斯拥有美国完整国家森林储存的三分之一碳。但美国农业部表示，他们希望取消无路区规则，以便让消防员进入扑灭野火，并移除他们所说的过时监管障碍。但阿拉斯加这一地区的许多人认为这是为了增加伐木。特朗普政府过去曾试图提高国家木材产量，特朗普政府的第一次任期仅在汤加斯暂时取消了该规则。

articles.title: Apocalyptic sci-fi novel 'The End of Everything' wins this year's Booker Prize
articles.dek: The End of Everything by British author M. John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize. In a statement, Mary Beard, chair of this year's judges, called it a book that turns you upside down, raises…

paragraphs.en: The End of Everything by British author M. John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize. In a statement, Mary Beard, chair of this year's judges, called it a book that turns you upside down, raises a wry smile – and surprisingly, given the subject matter, leaves you with a twinge of optimism."
paragraphs.zh: 英国作家M·约翰·哈里森的《万物的终结》获得了2026年布克奖。在一份声明中，今年评委会主席玛丽·比尔德称，这是一本会让你颠倒过来思考、露出苦笑——令人惊讶的是，考虑到主题，它还能让你感到一丝乐观的书。

paragraphs.en: The satirical sci-fi novel follows Philip, a man who looks for "artifacts" along the coast in Kent, England, and his aunt Marnie. The book is set in a post-apocalyptic future, dealing with the slow-burning invasion of the shape-shifting iGhetti.
paragraphs.zh: 这部讽刺性的科幻小说讲述了菲利普的故事，他是一个在英国肯特海岸寻找“文物”的人，以及他的姑妈玛妮。小说设定在末日后的未来，讲述了变形的iGhetti缓慢入侵的故事。

paragraphs.en: In an interview with the Booker Prize team, Harrison said he drew inspiration from current affairs: "What happens when all of our expectations and explanations of the world become an ongoing disaster, but we still have to make a life?"
paragraphs.zh: 在接受布克奖团队采访时，哈里森表示他从时事中获得灵感：“当我们对世界的所有期望和解释都变成持续的灾难时，我们仍然必须生活，这会发生什么？”

paragraphs.en: At 81, Harrison is the oldest author to win in the history of the prize. He's had a decades-long writing career, with Everything being his 13th novel. Most of his career has been spent writing science fiction. His 2006 novel, Nova Swing, won both the Arthur C. Clarke and Philip K. Dick awards (which reward the best in science fiction in the U.K. and U.S., respectively).
paragraphs.zh: 哈里森在81岁时成为该奖历史上最年长的获奖作家。他拥有长达数十年的写作生涯，《万物》是他的第13部小说。他的大部分职业生涯都专注于科幻写作。他2006年的小说《新星摇摆》赢得了阿瑟·C·克拉克奖和菲利普·K·迪克奖（分别奖励英国和美国的最佳科幻作品）。

paragraphs.en: "Many past Booker Prize authors have borrowed facets of science fiction in their work," wrote Gaby Wood, chief executive of the Booker Prize Foundation, in a statement. "But M. John Harrison is the first Booker winner to have emerged from the bona fide SF world. He is a genuinely original thinker, a genre-defying writer who takes ideas seriously."
paragraphs.zh: 布克奖基金会首席执行官加比·伍德在一份声明中写道：“许多过去的布克奖得主在他们的作品中借鉴了科幻小说的元素。但M. 约翰·哈里森是首位从真正的科幻世界中脱颖而出的布克奖得主。他是一个真正的原创思想者，一位超越类型的作家，认真对待思想。”

paragraphs.en: The Booker Prize honors the best fiction published in the U.K. and Ireland. Besides Beard, this year's judges included the poet Raymond Antrobus, Pulp frontman Jarvis Cocker, editor and critic Rebecca Liu, and poet and novelist Patricia Lockwood. The other books shortlisted for the prize this year included Marlon James' The Disappearers and The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout.
paragraphs.zh: 布克奖表彰在英国和爱尔兰出版的最佳小说。除了比尔德，今年的评委还包括诗人雷蒙德·安特鲁布斯（Raymond Antrobus）、Pulp乐队主唱贾维斯·考克（Jarvis Cocker）、编辑和评论家刘瑞贝卡（Rebecca Liu）、以及诗人兼小说家帕特里夏·洛克伍德（Patricia Lockwood）。今年入围该奖的其他书籍还包括马龙·詹姆斯（Marlon James）的《消失者》和伊丽莎白·斯特劳特（Elizabeth Strout）的《我们从未说过的事》。

paragraphs.en: Winners of the prize receive £50,000 (about $67,000), and a trophy presented by the previous year's winner. Author David Szalay won the 2025 prize with his novel Flesh.
paragraphs.zh: 获奖者将获得50,000英镑（约67,000美元）的奖金，以及由上一年获奖者颁发的奖杯。作家大卫·萨莱凭借他的小说《血肉》赢得了2025年的奖项。

articles.title: The world's largest telecoms firm is on trial and the outcome has global implications
articles.dek: Huawei, the world's biggest telecommunications company, is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions.

paragraphs.en: Huawei, the world's biggest telecommunications company, is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions.
paragraphs.zh: 华为，这家世界上最大的电信公司，正在纽约受审，被控窃取美国技术并规避美国制裁。

paragraphs.en: In a federal courtroom in Brooklyn, the world's biggest telecommunications company is on trial. Huawei is a Chinese firm that makes smartphones, laptops, routers and all sorts of telecoms equipment that's available all over the world. The U.S. has long alleged that Huawei products pose a security risk and have banned them from being sold in the United States. And according to the U.S. government, Huawei is also a criminal enterprise. U.S. prosecutors allege that Huawei built its telecoms empire by stealing from American companies and violated U.S. sanctions by doing business in Iran and North Korea. In 2018, this all came to a head.
paragraphs.zh: 在布鲁克林的联邦法庭上，世界上最大的电信公司正在受审。华为是一家中国公司，生产智能手机、笔记本电脑、路由器以及各种在全球范围内可用的电信设备。美国长期以来一直声称华为产品存在安全风险，并禁止其在美国销售。根据美国政府的说法，华为也是一个犯罪企业。美国检察官指控华为通过从美国公司窃取技术建立其电信帝国，并在伊朗和朝鲜开展业务，违反了美国的制裁。2018年，这一切达到了高潮。

paragraphs.en: UNIDENTIFIED REPORTER: Canadian authorities have arrested the chief financial officer of the Chinese telecommunications giant Huawei.
paragraphs.zh: 未具名记者：加拿大当局已逮捕中国电信巨头华为的首席财务官。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: In what is widely seen as an act of retaliation, China arrested two Canadians living in China, detaining them for nearly three years.
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：在广泛被视为报复的行为中，中国逮捕了两名居住在中国的加拿大人，并将他们拘留了近三年。

paragraphs.en: SCOTT SIMON, BYLINE: Late last night, China released two Canadian businessmen who had been imprisoned in China for more than a thousand days.
paragraphs.zh: 斯科特·西蒙, 报道：昨晚晚些时候，中国释放了两名在中国被监禁了超过一千天的加拿大商人。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: The U.S. agreed to a plea deal that freed Meng and released the two Canadians. One of them, Michael Kovrig, joins us now. Welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：美国同意了一项认罪协议，释放了孟晚舟并释放了两名加拿大人。其中一位，迈克尔·科夫里格，现在加入我们。欢迎。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So before we begin, I think it's worth doing a thorough introduction, so our audience understands exactly who you are and why we are talking to you. In 2018, you were living in China, working as an analyst for the nonprofit International Crisis Group. Then in December of that year, Chinese police arrested you on suspicion of espionage. You were held for nearly three years. It's been around five years since you were released. Why do you think the Chinese targeted you?
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：所以在我们开始之前，我认为有必要做一个彻底的介绍，让我们的观众确切了解你是谁，以及我们为什么要跟你谈话。2018年，你居住在中国，作为非营利组织国际危机组织的分析师工作。然后在那年的12月，中国警方以间谍活动的嫌疑逮捕了你。你被关押了将近三年。自你获释以来已经大约五年了。你认为中国为什么会针对你？

paragraphs.en: KOVRIG: It's a two-part question, Rob. The first is, why did they grab Canadians, and then why did they pick me specifically? So the Chinese Communist Party directed the Beijing State Security Bureau to abduct Canadians because they wanted to blackmail the Canadian government into releasing Meng Wanzhou. It was hostage diplomacy, that simple.
paragraphs.zh: KOVRIG：这是个两部分的问题，Rob。第一个是，他们为什么抓加拿大人，第二个是，为什么特别选中我？所以，中国共产党指示北京国家安全局绑架加拿大人，因为他们想通过勒索加拿大政府来释放孟晚舟。这就是人质外交，就这么简单。

articles.title: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
articles.dek: The share of first-time homebuyers remains at a near-record low of 22% as a housing shortage and high prices sideline many, according to a new report by the National Association of Realtors. But…

paragraphs.en: The share of first-time homebuyers remains at a near-record low of 22% as a housing shortage and high prices sideline many, according to a new report by the National Association of Realtors. But those who are managing to buy are older and wealthier than in the past, and 1 in 10 paid all cash, a record high since such data was collected starting in 2003.
paragraphs.zh: 根据全国房地产经纪人协会的一份新报告，由于住房短缺和高房价让许多人无法参与，首次购房者的比例仍维持在接近历史低点的22%。但那些能够购房的人比过去更年长且更富有，且每10个人中就有1人全款支付，这是自2003年开始收集此类数据以来的最高纪录。

paragraphs.en: "Inheritances are really driving this," said Jessica Lautz, deputy chief economist at the NAR.
paragraphs.zh: 全国房地产经纪人协会副首席经济学家杰西卡·劳茨表示：“遗产转让确实在推动这一进程。”

paragraphs.en: First-time buyers who paid all-cash were more likely than those who financed a house to use an inheritance (28%) or proceeds from the sale of an inherited property (21%). They were also older.
paragraphs.zh: 一次性付清现金的首次购房者，比那些贷款购房的人更可能使用遗产（28%）或出售继承财产的收益（21%）。他们的年龄也更大。

paragraphs.en: NAR finds the median age of all first-time buyers remains at 40, a record high. For first-time buyers who financed a purchase it was 38, while for those who paid all-cash it was 54. "They waited a significant period of time for that generational transfer of wealth to come through," Lautz said.
paragraphs.zh: NAR发现，所有首次购房者的中位年龄仍为40岁，创历史新高。对于通过融资购买的首次购房者，中位年龄为38岁，而全款购买者的中位年龄为54岁。Lautz表示：“他们等待了很长一段时间，才迎来这次代际财富的转移。”

paragraphs.en: For first-time buyers overall, personal savings was the biggest source of funding for a down payment. But in another shift, more people used assets – like a 401(k), stocks, or cryptocurrency – than financial help from family or friends. Older buyers have had more time to save up, Lautz said, but she thinks there's another factor: "I think it's uncomfortable to ask mom and dad for a gift or loan when you're hitting 40 versus your young 30s."
paragraphs.zh: 对于首次购房者而言，总体上个人储蓄是首付的最大资金来源。但另一方面，更多人使用资产——如401(k)账户、股票或加密货币——而非来自家人或朋友的经济帮助。Lautz表示，年长的购房者有更多时间积蓄，但她认为还有另一个因素：“我觉得当你四十岁左右时，向父母请求赠与或贷款会让人感到不舒服，而在三十出头时则没有这种感觉。”

paragraphs.en: The share of first time buyers using an inheritance is likely to grow in coming years as boomers reach their 80's and beyond. As the report noted, "there is a growing divide among those who are saving independently and priced out of homeownership, versus those who are waiting on the sidelines but then given a generational transfer of wealth."
paragraphs.zh: 随着婴儿潮一代步入80岁及以上，首次购房者使用遗产的比例在未来几年可能会增加。正如报告所指出的，“在那些独立储蓄却被房价排除在外的人群，与那些一直在旁观但随后获得代际财富转移的人群之间，分化日益加剧。”

paragraphs.en: Real estate agents around the country are seeing the change.
paragraphs.zh: 全国各地的房地产经纪人都在看到这个变化。

paragraphs.en: "I would say in the first 15 years of my career, I saw virtually zero first-time home buyers paying all cash," said Jason Miller, a broker with Trust Real Estate Company in St. Cloud, Minn.

articles.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue to block California youth social media law
articles.dek: Google, Meta, and TikTok have sued California to block the enforcement of a state law meant to protect children from getting addicted to social media.

paragraphs.en: Google, Meta, and TikTok have sued California to block the enforcement of a state law meant to protect children from getting addicted to social media.
paragraphs.zh: 谷歌、Meta 和抖音已起诉加利福尼亚州，以阻止执行一项旨在保护儿童免受社交媒体上瘾的州法律。

paragraphs.en: Google, Meta and TikTok sued the state of California this week to block a new law aimed at shielding youngsters from features of addictive social media. KQED's Rachael Myrow joins us. She's senior editor of member station KQED's Silicon Valley News Desk. And before we begin, we should note that Google is among NPR's financial supporters. Rachael, thanks so much for being with us.
paragraphs.zh: 本周，谷歌、Meta 和 TikTok 起诉了加利福尼亚州，试图阻止一项旨在保护青少年免受社交媒体成瘾功能影响的新法律。KQED 的 Rachael Myrow 加入了我们的讨论。她是 KQED 会员电台硅谷新闻台的高级编辑。在我们开始之前，我们应该指出，谷歌是 NPR 的财务支持者之一。Rachael，非常感谢你与我们一同参与讨论。

paragraphs.en: SIMON: First, please remind us about the law these companies are suing over. It was only signed in September - hasn't gone into effect yet. What's it supposed to do?
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：首先，请提醒我们一下这些公司正在起诉的法律。它只是九月份签署的——还没有生效。它应该起什么作用？

paragraphs.en: MYROW: The law goes into effect in January. It prohibits social media platforms from offering children under 16 things like personalized feeds and autoplay for videos. It also requires the deletion of children's accounts with those features. So in separate lawsuits filed in San Francisco, San Jose and Los Angeles, Meta, Google and TikTok respectively said the law wrongly compels them to honor California's preferred means of presenting content to children and substitutes the state's judgment for that of parents.
paragraphs.zh: MYROW：这项法律将于一月生效。它禁止社交媒体平台向16岁以下的儿童提供个性化信息流和视频自动播放等功能。它还要求删除拥有这些功能的儿童账户。因此，在旧金山、圣何塞和洛杉矶分别提起的诉讼中，Meta、谷歌和TikTok分别表示，这项法律错误地强制他们遵守加利福尼亚州对向儿童展示内容的偏好方式，并将该州的判断替代了父母的判断。

paragraphs.en: They also said the law violates First Amendment free-speech protections, as well as Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act. That broadly shields online platforms from liability over user content. The California attorney general's office wrote me that it is reviewing the lawsuits, adding, quote, "our office is committed to defending California's commonsense laws to protect kids online."
paragraphs.zh: 他们还表示，该法律侵犯了第一修正案的言论自由保护，以及联邦《通信体面法案》第230条。该条款广泛地保护在线平台免于对用户内容承担责任。加利福尼亚州总检察长办公室写信给我说，他们正在审查这些诉讼，并补充说，引用，“我们的办公室致力于维护加利福尼亚州保护儿童在线的常识性法律。”

paragraphs.en: SIMON: And, Rachael, I gather there are groups and individuals in the state who oppose this law when it's passed. What's been their reaction?
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：瑞切尔，我了解到在州内有一些团体和个人在这项法律通过时会反对它。他们的反应是什么？

paragraphs.en: MYROW: Well, one law professor here in Silicon Valley I talked to argued AB 1709 is filled with censorship problems. He's particularly worried about what I mentioned earlier - that the law requires these companies to delete children's accounts if the platforms refuse to withdraw the features that make them so addictive. From his perspective, that deprives those children of the ability to publish their own speech in really what has become the public square. Meta and TikTok echoed those arguments in email statements to KQED.
paragraphs.zh: MYROW：嗯，我在硅谷采访的一位法律教授认为 AB 1709 存在很多审查问题。他尤其担心我之前提到的——该法律要求这些公司如果平台拒绝撤销那些让孩子上瘾的功能，就必须删除儿童账号。在他看来，这剥夺了那些孩子在实际上已经成为公共广场的地方发表自己言论的能力。Meta 和 TikTok 在给 KQED 的电子邮件声明中也表达了类似的观点。

paragraphs.en: I also talked to the digital rights group the Electronic Frontier Foundation, which also lobbied in Sacramento against the bill. They want to see a comprehensive privacy law at the federal level that limits the data social media companies can collect, sell and use to hook consumers. The group isn't pro-Big Tech, but they don't like this law.
paragraphs.zh: 我还与数字权利组织电子前沿基金会（Electronic Frontier Foundation）进行了交谈，该组织也曾在萨克拉门托为反对该法案进行游说。他们希望在联邦层面看到一项全面的隐私法，限制社交媒体公司可以收集、出售和用于吸引消费者的数据。该组织并非支持大型科技公司，但他们不喜欢这项法律。

articles.title: SS United States, a historic ship will be sunk to create an artificial reef
articles.dek: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Alex Fogg, Natural Resources Chief of Okaloosa County, Florida, about efforts to deliberately sink the SS United States and create an artificial reef in its wreckage.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Alex Fogg, Natural Resources Chief of Okaloosa County, Florida, about efforts to deliberately sink the SS United States and create an artificial reef in its wreckage.
paragraphs.zh: NPR的艾莎·拉斯科（Ayesha Rascoe）与佛罗里达州奥卡卢萨县自然资源主管亚历克斯·福格（Alex Fogg）谈论了故意将美国号客轮沉入海中并在其残骸中创建人工珊瑚礁的努力。

paragraphs.en: A historic ship docked on the Gulf Coast is getting a second life by being put down, down as in the ocean floor. This Thursday, the SS United States will be sunk on purpose to create the largest artificial reef in the world near Destin, Florida. Joining me now is Alex Fogg, the natural resources chief for Okaloosa County, Florida. Thank you so much for joining us.
paragraphs.zh: 一艘停靠在墨西哥湾沿岸的历史船正通过被下沉，也就是下沉到海底，获得第二次生命。本周四，SS美国号将被故意沉没，以在佛罗里达州德斯廷附近创造世界上最大的人工礁。现在加入我们的是佛罗里达州奥卡卢萨县的自然资源主管亚历克斯·福格。非常感谢您的加入。

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: So first of all, tell us a little bit about the ship, its history and why it's so special.
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE：首先，请告诉我们一些关于这艘船的信息，它的历史以及为什么它如此特别。

paragraphs.en: FOGG: So the SS United States, it's huge. We've done a lot of artificial reef projects in the past, and this one really sticks out really 'cause of its size, but also its storied past. It's a vessel that was built back in the early 1950s, went back and forth to Europe. It was eventually retired in the late 1960s when air travel just became so much more efficient. But during that time, it carried all sorts of really famous people and was geared to be a troop carrier in the event of the United States getting involved in another world war.
paragraphs.zh: FOGG：所以SS United States号，非常巨大。我们过去做过很多人工礁项目，而这个项目确实非常突出，不仅因为它的规模，还因为它丰富的历史。这是一艘建造于20世纪50年代初的船，往返欧洲。到了20世纪60年代末，由于航空旅行变得更加高效，它最终退役。但在那段时间，它运载过各种非常有名的人物，并且在美国卷入另一场世界大战的情况下，还被设计成可以运送军队的船只。

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: My understanding is that it sat for decades in Philadelphia and made its way around the world, as you talked about. But then eventually down to Florida. How did it get down to Florida?
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE：我理解的是，它在费城搁置了数十年，然后像你说的那样辗转世界各地。但最终到了佛罗里达州。它是怎么到佛罗里达的？

paragraphs.en: FOGG: Yeah. It was a very long tow. So we had to do a lot of checks and balances with our contractor, naval architects, U.S. Coast Guard, all sorts of different entities, to make sure that it was seaworthy enough to be towed from Philadelphia all the way down to Mobile, Alabama, where the full remediation was going to occur.
paragraphs.zh: FOGG：是的。这是一次非常长的拖航。因此我们不得不与我们的承包商、海军建筑师、美国海岸警卫队以及各种不同的机构进行大量的检查和平衡，以确保它足够适航，能够从费城拖到阿拉巴马州的莫比尔，在那里将进行全面的修复。

paragraphs.en: RASCOE: Well, let's talk about the big plans for the ship's new life. Like, why would you sink a nearly 900-foot ship intentionally in the Gulf of Mexico?
paragraphs.zh: RASCOE：好吧，让我们谈谈这艘船新生活的大计划。比如，为什么你要故意把一艘接近900英尺的船沉在墨西哥湾？

paragraphs.en: FOGG: We tried to talk about or tried to figure out ways that we could increase our artificial reef construction to benefit tourism, to benefit the environment. Came up with a whole plan to acquire a bunch of vessels to sink as artificial reefs 'cause when people come diving in a destination, they don't want to dive, you know, sand, or maybe don't want to dive natural reefs all the time. They want to be a bona fide wreck diver. So by deploying these wrecks, it started to put us on the map as a dive destination, and there was a plan that if a vessel of very large size or a very cool story comes along, we would pursue it. And the SS United States was that ship.
paragraphs.zh: FOGG：我们尝试讨论或尝试找出方法来增加人工礁的建设，以惠及旅游业和环境。我们制定了一个完整的计划，打算收购一批船只用于沉入海中作为人工礁，因为当人们去某个地方潜水时，他们不想潜入沙地，或者有时不总是想潜自然礁。他们想成为真正的沉船潜水者。所以通过部署这些沉船，我们开始在潜水目的地上打响了名声，而且有一个计划，如果出现一艘非常大或故事非常特别的船，我们会去争取。而“美利坚号”就是那艘船。

articles.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina
articles.dek: FLORIDA, Uruguay — Pope Leo XIV wrapped up his visit to Uruguay on Sunday by praising the women who have passed the Catholic faith onto younger generations, as he highlighted the role the church…

paragraphs.en: FLORIDA, Uruguay — Pope Leo XIV wrapped up his visit to Uruguay on Sunday by praising the women who have passed the Catholic faith onto younger generations, as he highlighted the role the church has played since the founding of Latin America's most secular country.
paragraphs.zh: 乌拉圭，佛罗里达——教皇利奥十四世在周日结束对乌拉圭的访问时，赞扬了那些将天主教信仰传给年轻一代的女性，并强调了教会自拉丁美洲最世俗国家建国以来所发挥的作用。

paragraphs.en: Leo traveled to the city of Florida, north of Montevideo, to mark an important Catholic feast day before heading to Argentina for the second leg of his South American tour. It's expected to be the most politically delicate stop, given the Catholic Church's sharp criticisms of the austerity program of libertarian President Javier Milei.
paragraphs.zh: Leo 前往位于蒙得维的北方的佛罗里达市，以纪念一个重要的天主教节日，然后前往阿根廷进行他南美之旅的第二站。考虑到天主教会对自由主义总统哈维尔·米莱的紧缩计划提出了尖锐批评，这一站预计将是政治上最为敏感的。

paragraphs.en: For his final event in Uruguay, Leo celebrated the feast of the Virgin of the Thirty-three. According to tradition, 33 independence patriots acquired the Guaraní statue and had it with them when independence was declared from the Brazilian empire in Florida on Aug. 25, 1825.
paragraphs.zh: 在乌拉圭的最后一场活动中，莱奥庆祝了三十三圣母节。根据传统，33位独立爱国者获得了瓜拉尼圣像，并在1825年8月25日从巴西帝国在佛罗里达宣布独立时随身携带它。

paragraphs.en: Leo became the first pope in nearly four decades to visit Uruguay, in hopes of reminding its people that the Catholic Church is part of their very identity as a nation — even if, in subsequent decades, the country went on a deeply secular, and at times anticlerical, route.
paragraphs.zh: 莱奥成为近四十年来首位访问乌拉圭的教皇，希望提醒乌拉圭人民，天主教会是他们作为一个国家身份的一部分——即使在随后的几十年里，该国走上了深度世俗化，有时甚至反教士的道路。

paragraphs.en: In his homily, delivered in front of Florida's cathedral, Leo recalled the presence of the statue at the time of independence in reminding Uruguayans that "the history of peoples, too, cannot be fully understood without reference to God," and especially a mother.
paragraphs.zh: 在他于佛罗里达大教堂前发表的讲道中，列奥回忆起独立时雕像的存在，提醒乌拉圭人，“没有提到上帝，民族的历史也无法被完全理解”，尤其是一位母亲。

paragraphs.en: He thanked all the mothers and grandmothers who have passed the faith onto younger generations, and acknowledged their pain when their efforts didn't stick.
paragraphs.zh: 他感谢了所有将信仰传给下一代的母亲和祖母，并认可了当她们的努力未能成功时所经历的痛苦。

paragraphs.en: "You taught your children to pray, and today they no longer do so. You used to attend Mass together, and it has been years since they entered a church," he said. But he urged them to not despair.
paragraphs.zh: “你教你的孩子们祈祷，但今天他们已经不再祈祷。你们曾经一起去做弥撒，但他们已经多年没有进入教堂了，”他说。但他鼓励他们不要绝望。

paragraphs.en: "Mothers and grandmothers: never tire of passing on the faith!"
paragraphs.zh: 母亲和祖母：永远不要厌倦传递信仰！

articles.title: Israeli president invites Netanyahu's opposition leader to broker new government
articles.dek: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.

paragraphs.en: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.
paragraphs.zh: 随着总统赫尔佐格将组建政府的任务交给反对派领导人加迪·艾森科特，以色列的政治格局发生变化，这对本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的权力掌控造成打击。

paragraphs.en: Israel's president says he's tapped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, to form the next Israeli government. Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot won a clear majority in last month's election. But parties representing most of the members of Israel's parliament have recommended Eisenkot to try to form a governing coalition. For more on what that means, let's go to NPR's Lauren Frayer, who joins us live from Tel Aviv. Hey, Lauren.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列总统表示，他已任命总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的政治对手加迪·艾森科特组建下一届以色列政府。上个月的选举中，内塔尼亚胡和艾森科特都未获得明确多数。但代表以色列议会大多数成员的政党已推荐艾森科特尝试组建执政联盟。关于这意味着什么，让我们连线NPR的劳伦·弗雷耶，她正在特拉维夫为我们进行现场报道。嗨，劳伦。

paragraphs.en: FRAYER: So he's a former military chief whose son was an Israeli soldier killed in combat in Gaza. He is a center-right politician, while Netanyahu is on the far right. Eisenkot briefly served in Netanyahu's cabinet after the October 7 Hamas attacks on Israel, but the two had a falling out. Eisenkot founded a new political party, ran against Netanyahu and now wants to replace him. Netanyahu's been Israel's longest serving prime minister, and he is still the caretaker prime minister for now.
paragraphs.zh: FRAYER：所以他是一位前军事首长，他的儿子是以色列士兵，在加沙作战中阵亡。他是一位中右翼政治家，而内塔尼亚胡则属于极右翼。以色列的伊森科特在10月7日哈马斯袭击以色列后曾短暂担任内塔尼亚胡内阁成员，但两人后来关系破裂。伊森科特创立了一个新政党，竞选反对内塔尼亚胡，现在想取代他。内塔尼亚胡是以色列任职时间最长的总理，目前仍是看守总理。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: Got it. So what is the timeline for a possible change of power here?
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：明白。那么这里可能更换权力的时间表是什么？

paragraphs.en: FRAYER: Israel's president is holding a ceremony with Eisenkot Sunday evening local time, and that's when the clock starts. Eisenkot has about six weeks to form a coalition with other parties. If he fails, the president could ask someone else to try, perhaps Netanyahu. If that person fails, Israel could be looking at do-over elections in a few months. And the coalition building could be really tough.
paragraphs.zh: FRAYER：以色列总统将于当地时间周日晚与艾森科特举行仪式，届时计时开始。艾森科特大约有六周时间与其他政党组建联盟。如果他失败，总统可能会请别人尝试组建，也许是内塔尼亚胡。如果那个人也失败，以色列可能在几个月内面临重新选举。而组建联盟可能会非常困难。

paragraphs.en: FRAYER: So a coalition would include all these strange bedfellows, you know, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties to Arab-led parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel. They make up about 20% of Israel and had a record turnout in these elections - could be the kingmakers. But both Eisenkot and Netanyahu ruled out working with them. And now there's some public pressure on Eisenkot to change his mind. Tonight, Netanyahu issued a video warning against that, against partnering what - with what he called Hamas supporters and, quote, "those who oppose Judaism." You know, Netanyahu has used a lot of racist and Islamophobic language throughout this election towards the - Israel's minority-Arab population. Eisenkot tonight called Netanyahu's video hysterical. So things are very, very tense here.
paragraphs.zh: FRAYER：所以一个联盟会包括所有这些奇怪的政治伙伴，你知道的，从极端正统犹太党派到代表以色列巴勒斯坦公民的阿拉伯领导党派。他们大约占以色列人口的20%，在这次选举中创下了投票记录——可能成为关键决策者。但艾森科特和内塔尼亚胡都排除了与他们合作的可能性。现在，对艾森科特有一些公众压力，要求他改变主意。今晚，内塔尼亚胡发布了一段视频，警告不要这样做，不要与——也就是他所谓的哈马斯支持者以及“那些反对犹太教的人”合作。你知道，内塔尼亚胡在这次选举中对以色列少数阿拉伯人口使用了很多种族主义和伊斯兰恐惧的言辞。艾森科特今晚称内塔尼亚胡的视频为歇斯底里。所以这里的局势非常，非常紧张。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: Yeah, it sounds like it. I mean, so the next Israeli prime minister will also have to contend with a more strained relationship with the United States. And I'm curious here, how did the U.S. midterm election results go over in Israel?
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：是的，听起来是这样。我的意思是，下一任以色列总理也将不得不应对与美国关系更加紧张的问题。我很好奇，美国中期选举的结果在以色列反响如何？

paragraphs.en: FRAYER: Pretty badly. I mean, many Israelis I've talked to are really dismayed that criticism of Israel was a talking point for some of the winning candidates in the U.S. You know, newspapers here are splashed with photos of the Democratic senator-elect from Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed. Meanwhile, President Trump on Election Day says he's cutting U.S. aid to Israel.
paragraphs.zh: FRAYER：相当糟糕。我的意思是，我交谈过的许多以色列人真的很沮丧，因为对以色列的批评成为了一些美国当选候选人的讨论话题。你知道，这里的报纸上满是密歇根州当选民主党参议员阿卜杜勒·艾尔-赛义德的照片。与此同时，特朗普总统在选举日表示，他将削减对以色列的美国援助。

articles.dek: Scammers can even make money off of people starved for FAN fiction. That's my takeaway from a fake website popping up that tried to sell computer-generated audiobooks of fan fiction, which is…

paragraphs.en: Scammers can even make money off of people starved for FAN fiction. That's my takeaway from a fake website popping up that tried to sell computer-generated audiobooks of fan fiction, which is content created by ANYONE based off of existing works. "Fifty Shades of Grey" started as a fanfic of Twilight, for example.
paragraphs.zh: 骗子甚至可以从渴望同人小说的人身上赚钱。这是我从一个出现的假网站中的体会，该网站试图出售由计算机生成的同人小说有声书。同人小说是任何人基于现有作品创作的内容。例如，《五十度灰》最初就是《暮光之城》的同人作品。

paragraphs.en: This scam website popped up in the wake of the uber-popular fan fiction website AO3, Archive of our Own, going down for an estimated two to four weeks after a "security incident." People are starved for their stories and apparently will click on anything. Lucky for the world, the scam website has been taken down.
paragraphs.zh: 在超受欢迎的同人小说网站AO3（Archive of Our Own）因一次“安全事件”预计停摆两到四周后，这个诈骗网站就出现了。人们对他们的故事渴望不已，显然会点击任何东西。幸运的是，这个诈骗网站已经被关闭。

paragraphs.en: What to know: North Korea just loves stealing crypto. They love it! It's become a major part of their economy. Last week, a state-sponsored hacking group called "TraderTraitor" executed the largest crypto theft in history, stealing $6.43 billion from Binance, a massive cryptocurrency exchange. $2.85 billion has been frozen or seized, according to Elliptic, a crypto analytics & compliance firm. But $3.35 billion is still linked to the group. "TraderTraitor" is actively trying to launder this money (yes, crypto is surprisingly traceable). A huge part of the stolen funds are in stablecoin, which can be frozen. Whatever isn't already frozen, the hacking group is trying to launder it and FAST. So how are they doing it?
paragraphs.zh: 需要了解的是：朝鲜非常喜欢盗取加密货币。他们非常热衷！这已经成为他们经济的重要组成部分。上周，一个名为“TraderTraitor”的国家支持的黑客组织实施了史上最大规模的加密货币盗窃，从大型加密货币交易所币安窃取了64.3亿美元。据加密分析与合规公司Elliptic称，其中28.5亿美元已被冻结或被没收。但仍有33.5亿美元与该组织有关联。“TraderTraitor”正在积极尝试洗钱（是的，加密货币出乎意料地可追踪）。被盗资金中很大一部分是稳定币，可以被冻结。尚未被冻结的部分，该黑客组织正在尝试快速洗钱。那么，他们是如何做到的呢？

paragraphs.en: How are the criminals laundering these assets?: Laundering this much crypto is NOT simple. The intelligence firm Elliptic broke down how "TraderTraitor" is trying to quickly protect its newfound loot. First of all, they want to turn any Stablecoin into assets that cannot be frozen, like Ether (ETH). From there, the group is using automation to create LOTS of new wallets to filter small amounts of crypto, so as not to trigger alarms for moving assets worth a bazillion dollars. From there, launderers want to move the money across networks like Ethereum to Bitcoin then pull it from a mixed pool with a bunch of other people's assets. The goal: make the crypto's origins hazy. "TraderTraitor" is moving fast. On Tuesday, Elliptic reported the group has made more than 40,000 transactions, creating a new wallet every 25 seconds.
paragraphs.zh: 罪犯是如何洗这些资产的？：洗这么多加密货币并不简单。情报公司 Elliptic 分析了“TraderTraitor”是如何试图快速保护其新获得的赃款的。首先，他们希望将任何稳定币转换为无法被冻结的资产，比如以太坊（ETH）。接下来，该组织使用自动化工具创建大量新钱包来过滤少量加密货币，以避免触发价值数万亿美元资产转移的警报。之后，洗钱者希望将资金从以太坊网络转移到比特币网络，然后从一个混合池中取出资金，该池还包含其他人的资产。目标：让加密货币的来源变得模糊。“TraderTraitor”动作很快。周二，Elliptic 报告称，该组织已经进行了超过 40,000 笔交易，每 25 秒创建一个新钱包。

paragraphs.en: One interesting detail: Binance has promised to make customers whole, but investors have already pulled billions from the exchange.
paragraphs.zh: 一个有趣的细节：币安承诺会让客户得到赔偿，但投资者已经从该交易所撤出了数十亿美元。

paragraphs.en: What to know: This week, gold fell below $4,000 per ounce after hitting nearly $5,600 per ounce in January. It's typically seen as a safe-haven asset, which is why investors were shoveling money into it earlier this year. As you know, things have been a bit volatile from the Iran War to the criminal probe into the Federal Reserve chair. But today, there's still economic uncertainty, no? The war with Iran rages on. So why are gold prices falling? I took my question to Planet Money co-host Jeff Guo to find out. I asked him: could gold be going down because Treasury bond yields are up? That could mean there are MORE reliable ways to make money.
paragraphs.zh: 需要了解的情况：本周，黄金价格跌破每盎司4,000美元，此前在1月份曾接近每盎司5,600美元。黄金通常被视为避险资产，这就是为什么投资者今年早些时候纷纷投入资金的原因。正如你所知，从伊朗战争到对美联储主席的刑事调查，情况一直有些波动。但今天，经济仍然存在不确定性，不是吗？与伊朗的战争仍在继续。那么，为什么黄金价格会下跌呢？我把这个问题带给了Planet Money的联合主持人郭杰夫（Jeff Guo）了解情况。我问他：黄金价格下跌是否可能是因为国债收益率上升？这可能意味着存在更可靠的赚钱方式。

paragraphs.en: Jeff: I think you are right that rising Treasury yields are the story. As you know, gold tends to be seen as a "safe" asset and an inflation hedge; but the problem is that gold doesn't earn any income/interest on its own. Meanwhile, you could buy a 10 year TIPS (Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities) bond right now that does earn income, above and beyond inflation. Sure, the Iran war is a source of political instability that might drive investors toward gold. But the main effect of the war so far seems to be raising the price of oil. And higher oil prices are one of the factors pushing interest rates up, making bonds more attractive relative to gold.
paragraphs.zh: 杰夫：我认为你说得对，国债收益率上升才是关键因素。正如你所知道的，黄金通常被视为“安全”资产和通胀对冲工具；但问题是，黄金本身不会产生任何收益/利息。与此同时，你现在可以买一只10年期的TIPS（国债抗通胀证券）债券，它确实能产生收益，而且超过通胀。当然，伊朗战争带来的政治不稳定可能会促使投资者转向黄金。但到目前为止，这场战争的主要影响似乎是推高了油价。而油价上涨是推动利率上升的因素之一，这使得债券相对于黄金更具吸引力。

articles.title: An unexpected activist emerged to help block a $5 billion data center in Maryland
articles.dek: The overgrown grass and weeds seem to stretch into the horizon on nearly 90 acres of empty land in Landover, Md. It used to be Landover Mall, but that closed in 2002, and the site has been mostly…

paragraphs.en: The overgrown grass and weeds seem to stretch into the horizon on nearly 90 acres of empty land in Landover, Md. It used to be Landover Mall, but that closed in 2002, and the site has been mostly vacant since.
paragraphs.zh: 在马里兰州兰多弗，近90英亩的空地上，杂草丛生的草地似乎延伸到地平线。这里曾是兰多弗购物中心，但该购物中心在2002年关闭，此后这一地块大部分时间处于空置状态。

paragraphs.en: In 2024, the developer that built the mall won approval from county planners for a $5 billion data center campus, and word began spreading through the largely Black community nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 在2024年，建造该商场的开发商获得县规划人员批准建设一个价值50亿美元的数据中心园区，并且消息开始在附近以黑人为主的社区中传播。

paragraphs.en: "I was like, 'Oh, hell no,'" said Taylor Frazier McCollum, describing the moment she learned about the project. She lived less than a mile away from it. "Why would you want to bring water-polluting, diesel-generating data centers right down the street from where people live, work, play? It just didn't make sense to me."
paragraphs.zh: 泰勒·弗雷泽·麦考勒姆（Taylor Frazier McCollum）描述她得知这个项目的那一刻时说：“我当时心想，‘哦，绝对不行。’”她住在离项目不到一英里的地方。“你为什么要在居民、工作和娱乐区的街道附近建造会污染水源、产生柴油的数据信息中心呢？我根本不理解。”

paragraphs.en: Frazier McCollum is one of a number of Americans whose political awakening was triggered by data center development. Across the country, community members have taken to local council hearings to voice their opposition. They've prompted — though estimates vary — about 500 moratoriums on data centers nationwide.
paragraphs.zh: 弗雷泽·麦考勒姆是一些因数据中心开发而政治觉醒的美国人之一。在全国各地，社区成员纷纷出席地方议会听证会表达他们的反对意见。他们促使——尽管估算有所不同——全国大约有500个关于数据中心的暂停建设令。

paragraphs.en: Unlike a lot of land-use activists trying to protect their homes from threats in their backyards, Frazier McCollum does not own a home. In 2024, she and her young daughter were evicted from their apartment. She was working at a waxing center that cut wages, and she could no longer cover her rent.
paragraphs.zh: 与许多试图保护自家后院免受威胁的土地使用活动家不同，弗雷泽·麦考勒姆没有房子。在2024年，她和她的小女儿被赶出了公寓。她当时在一家脱毛中心工作，但该公司降低了工资，她再也无法支付房租。

paragraphs.en: "It was difficult," Frazier McCollum recalled. "Because I created the ideal life paying for us to live in this apartment and have our own space ... and then to have it taken away ... It felt like something that wasn't ever going to end."
paragraphs.zh: “很困难，”弗雷泽·麦考勒姆回忆道。“因为我创造了理想的生活，支付我们住在这间公寓并拥有自己的空间……然后它被夺走了……感觉像是永远不会结束的事情。”

paragraphs.en: They've moved around and were living in her grandfather's home when she learned about the proposed project less than a mile away.
paragraphs.zh: 他们搬来搬去，并住在她爷爷的家里，当她得知不到一英里外的拟建项目时。

paragraphs.en: She created a petition that gathered over 25,000 signatures, leading to widely attended protests and culminating in multiple local moratoriums imposed on data centers throughout the county. It blocked the $5 billion project that was set to break ground between 2026 and 2027.
paragraphs.zh: 她发起了一份请愿书，收集了超过25,000个签名，导致大量人参与的抗议活动，并最终在全县对数据中心实施了多项地方性暂停令。它阻止了原定于2026年至2027年开工的50亿美元项目。
