articles.title: Trump says he's ending restrictions on climate-warming methane from oil drilling
articles.dek: BILLINGS, Mont. — President Donald Trump said Tuesday that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.

paragraphs.en: BILLINGS, Mont. — President Donald Trump said Tuesday that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.
paragraphs.zh: 蒙大拿州比林斯——总统唐纳德·特朗普周二表示，他的政府正在“终止”拜登时期的一项规则，该规则旨在减少石油和天然气钻探产生的温室气体甲烷排放。

paragraphs.en: Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save companies and consumers billions of dollars and unlock 210 million barrels of oil. That's equivalent to about 10 days of U.S. petroleum consumption.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普在德克萨斯州的一次竞选集会上表示，这一变化将为公司和消费者节省数十亿美元，并释放出2.1亿桶石油。这相当于美国约10天的石油消耗量。

paragraphs.en: The move aims to encourage more domestic drilling as Trump faces criticism over high fuel prices amid the war in Iran.
paragraphs.zh: 此举旨在鼓励更多的国内钻探，因为特朗普在伊朗战争期间因高燃料价格而面临批评。

paragraphs.en: Methane is responsible for about a third of planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions, scientists estimate.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家估计，甲烷约占导致地球变暖的温室气体排放的三分之一。

paragraphs.en: Cuts in methane emissions have emerged in recent years as a global priority to slow the rate of climate change. Oil and gas operations are the largest industrial source of methane, which is the main component in natural gas and far more potent to the atmosphere than carbon dioxide in the short term.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，减少甲烷排放已成为全球的优先事项，以减缓气候变化的速度。石油和天然气作业是最大的工业甲烷来源，甲烷是天然气的主要成分，在短期内对大气的影响远比二氧化碳更强。

paragraphs.en: The invisible gas leaks from equipment and is released into the atmosphere or burned off as a waste product by oil drillers.
paragraphs.zh: 这种看不见的气体从设备中泄漏，并被释放到大气中，或被石油钻探工作为废弃物燃烧掉。

paragraphs.en: Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin previewed the changes last month, saying they would eliminate the agency's "Super Emitter Program" that requires companies to investigate and repair major methane releases from oil and natural gas facilities. The agency would also set less restrictive standards for small oil and gas wells.
paragraphs.zh: 环境保护局局长李·泽尔丁上个月预览了这些变化，他表示，这些变化将取消该机构的“超级排放者计划”，该计划要求公司调查并修复油气设施的大量甲烷泄漏。该机构还将为小型油气井设定较少限制的标准。

paragraphs.en: Trump said during Tuesday's rally in Lubbock for Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton that Biden's plan "crushed the small operators" with crippling regulations.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普在周二为德克萨斯州共和党参议员候选人肯·帕克斯顿在拉伯克举行的集会上表示，拜登的计划“用严苛的法规压垮了小型运营商”。

articles.title: Pope Leo begins a 12-day, 3-country South America tour after his cancer surgery
articles.dek: MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay — Pope Leo XIV has arrived in South America for a 12-day, three-country journey that will be his longest and most far-reaching trip yet, and his first major overseas visit…

paragraphs.en: MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay — Pope Leo XIV has arrived in South America for a 12-day, three-country journey that will be his longest and most far-reaching trip yet, and his first major overseas visit since undergoing lung cancer surgery.
paragraphs.zh: 乌拉圭蒙得维的亚——教皇利奥十四世已抵达南美，开始为期12天、跨越三个国家的行程，这将是他迄今为止最长、范围最广的访问，也是他肺癌手术后的首次重大海外访问。

paragraphs.en: Along the way Leo will take 12 flights, including two helicopter rides, give 36 speeches and visit 10 cities including Cusco, Peru, which sits more than 11,000 feet above sea level. Even the heartiest of travelers can experience altitude sickness there and may require supplemental oxygen.
paragraphs.zh: 沿途，Leo将乘坐12次航班，包括两次直升机飞行，发表36场演讲，并访问包括秘鲁库斯科在内的10个城市，库斯科的海拔超过11,000英尺。即使是最强健的旅行者在那里也可能出现高原反应，可能需要额外的氧气。

paragraphs.en: Last month, Leo underwent surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung. Vatican officials say he has completed his two-week recovery period and requires no further treatment.
paragraphs.zh: 上个月，利奥接受了手术，切除了右肺的下叶。梵蒂冈官员表示，他已完成为期两周的康复期，不需要进一步治疗。

paragraphs.en: The Vatican's new communications chief Maria Montserrat Alvarado said the pontiff was eager to begin his journey. "His doctors are very confident and he'll have plenty of medical care on board should something happen," she said.
paragraphs.zh: 梵蒂冈新任通讯主管玛丽亚·蒙特塞拉特·阿尔瓦拉多表示，教皇迫切希望开始他的旅程。她说：“他的医生非常有信心，如果发生什么情况，他将在船上得到充足的医疗护理。”

paragraphs.en: A proposed papal address to the parliament triggered a swift rebuke from the public and politicians alike and was quickly scrapped. Instead, Uruguay's left-wing President Yamandú Orsi presided over the welcome ceremony outside Montevideo's main cathedral.
paragraphs.zh: 一份拟议中的教皇致议会的演讲稿引发了公众和政界人士的迅速谴责，并很快被撤回。取而代之的是，乌拉圭的左翼总统亚曼杜·奥尔西在蒙得维的亚主教座堂外主持了欢迎仪式。

paragraphs.en: Crowds of up to 30,000 people, according to the Vatican, had lined the streets to catch a glimpse of Pope Leo as he drove past in his Popemobile.
paragraphs.zh: 根据梵蒂冈的说法，多达三万人在街上排队，只为一睹教皇利奥乘坐教皇专车经过时的风采。

paragraphs.en: But the crowd gathered to greet him at the central Plaza Independencia was much smaller, not even filling half the length of the vast square. Those who came were nonetheless delighted to see him and hear his message.
paragraphs.zh: 但在独立广场中央迎接他的群众要小得多，甚至连广场的一半长度都没有填满。不过，那些前来的人仍然很高兴看到他并听到他的讲话。

paragraphs.en: The Pope wasted little time addressing Uruguay's secular traditions and its liberal laws on abortion and euthanasia. Uruguay was the first country in Latin America to legalize euthanasia through legislation, and, in 2012, became the second in the region to legalize abortion, after Cuba.
paragraphs.zh: 教皇几乎没有花时间就乌拉圭的世俗传统以及其关于堕胎和安乐死的自由法律发表看法。乌拉圭是拉丁美洲第一个通过立法使安乐死合法化的国家，并且在2012年成为该地区继古巴之后第二个使堕胎合法化的国家。

articles.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
articles.dek: Arab parties hold the key to power in deadlocked Israel election

paragraphs.en: Arab parties hold the key to power in deadlocked Israel election
paragraphs.zh: 阿拉伯政党掌握以色列僵局选举中的权力关键

paragraphs.en: KUFR QASI, Israel — In recent years many Palestinian citizens of Israel shunned elections, believing there was little to gain from participating in the politics of a state which, they say, regularly marginalizes their communities and oppresses their fellow Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
paragraphs.zh: 库夫尔卡西，以色列——近年来，许多以色列的巴勒斯坦公民回避选举，认为参与一个他们说经常边缘化自己的社区并压迫约旦河西岸和加沙地区同行巴勒斯坦人的国家的政治，没有什么可获得的。

paragraphs.en: But last month, Palestinian Arabs in Israel came to the ballot boxes in record numbers, helping strip Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's most far-right government in Israel's history of its majority, and giving Arab-led parties the votes they needed to become a powerful force in Israeli politics.
paragraphs.zh: 但在上个月，居住在以色列的巴勒斯坦阿拉伯人大规模前往投票站，以创纪录的方式投票，这帮助剥夺了本杰明·内塔尼亚胡担任的以色列历史上最极右政府的多数席位，并为阿拉伯主导的政党提供了他们在以色列政治中成为一个强大力量所需的选票。

paragraphs.en: "We blocked the government of Netanyahu from continuing," said Jamal Zahalka, chairman of the High Follow-Up Committee, the main umbrella body representing Palestinian citizens of Israel. "It's a historical achievement. I think our community found its strength."
paragraphs.zh: “我们阻止了内塔尼亚胡政府的继续执政，”高级跟进委员会主席贾迈勒·扎哈尔卡说，该委员会是代表以色列巴勒斯坦公民的主要伞形机构。“这是一个历史性的成就。我认为我们的社区找到了自己的力量。”

paragraphs.en: Neither Netanyahu's coalition, nor his main challenger Gadi Eisenkot's center-right opposition, reached the threshold of 61 seats needed to form a government. Arab-led parties won 19 out of 120 seats — enough to give them a critical role in the negotiations that will now determine who governs Israel at this turbulent moment in the country's history.
paragraphs.zh: 无论是内塔尼亚胡的联盟，还是他主要的对手加迪·艾森科特领导的中右翼反对派，都未能达到组建政府所需的61个席位门槛。由阿拉伯人领导的政党赢得了120个席位中的19个——足以使他们在谈判中发挥关键作用，而这些谈判将决定在以色列历史这个动荡时刻谁来执政。

paragraphs.en: The election results strike at the heart of the decades-long questions about how Israel defines itself and the role of Palestinian Arabs in its society.
paragraphs.zh: 选举结果触及了关于以色列如何定义自身以及巴勒斯坦阿拉伯人在其社会中角色的长期问题的核心。

paragraphs.en: At a park in the Palestinian-majority town of Kufr Qasim two days after the election, hundreds of people gathered for the annual commemoration of residents gunned down in 1956 by Israeli border police on the opening day of the Suez Crisis in the violent early years of the state, when Israel, Britain and France attacked Egypt after it nationalized the Suez Canal.
paragraphs.zh: 在选举两天后的巴勒斯坦人占多数的库夫尔卡西姆镇的一座公园里，数百人聚集在一起，参加年度纪念活动，以缅怀1956年以色列边境警察在苏伊士运河危机开端当天枪杀的居民。那是以色列建国初期的动荡岁月，当时以色列、英国和法国在埃及将苏伊士运河国有化后对埃及发起了攻击。

paragraphs.en: "And today we stand here, 70 years later," the speaker told the large crowd from a podium: "And the story still isn't over."
paragraphs.zh: 演讲者站在讲台上对聚集的大群人说：“而今天，70年过去了，我们依然站在这里，故事还没有结束。”

articles.title: This was the week the AI trade cracked. So what's next?
articles.dek: Big losses by AI shares in stock markets after Democrats won the midterm elections have left investors shaken and wondering comes next.

paragraphs.en: Big losses by AI shares in stock markets after Democrats won the midterm elections have left investors shaken and wondering comes next.
paragraphs.zh: 在中期选举中民主党获胜后，人工智能股票在股市中遭遇重大损失，这让投资者感到震惊并在思考接下来会发生什么。

paragraphs.en: It has been a bumpy ride for AI and tech stocks this week. AI shares bounced back today. That was after suffering a huge loss yesterday that wiped out more than $2 trillion in value. Big Democratic victories have raised big fears about the outlook for AI, which, of course, is a game-changing technology, and tech companies are pouring a ton of money into developing it. It's not clear, though, if we are in the middle of a tech bubble that is about to burst.
paragraphs.zh: 本周人工智能和科技股经历了颠簸的一周。今天，人工智能股票反弹了。在昨天遭受了巨大损失之后，这些损失抹去了超过2万亿美元的市值。民主党取得重大胜利，引发了人们对人工智能前景的巨大担忧。当然，人工智能是一项改变游戏规则的技术，而科技公司正在投入大量资金进行开发。不过，目前尚不清楚我们是否正处在即将破裂的科技泡沫之中。

paragraphs.en: Let's bring in NPR senior economics and finance editor Rafael Nam and NPR tech correspondent John Ruwitch. Hey to the both of you.
paragraphs.zh: 让我们请来NPR高级经济与金融编辑拉斐尔·纳姆以及NPR科技记者约翰·鲁维奇。向你们两位打个招呼。

paragraphs.en: KELLY: Hey. Rafael, you start. AI shares did recover today. Let's underscore that. But investors are still feeling queasy.
paragraphs.zh: 凯利：嘿，拉斐尔，你先说。人工智能股票今天确实回升了。我们要强调这一点。但是投资者仍然感到不安。

paragraphs.en: NAM: Yeah, I think the scale of the losses yesterday was pretty staggering. And another kind you see - the kind you only see every once in a while, to be honest. And investors are still a little shaken. I mean, traders had already been feeling very uneasy all year long about the AI trade, and there's a lot of money riding on AI.
paragraphs.zh: NAM：是的，我认为昨天的损失规模相当惊人。你还看到另一种情况——说实话，这种情况很少见。投资者们仍然有些震惊。我的意思是，交易员们整整一年对人工智能交易一直感到非常不安，而在人工智能上押注的资金很大。

paragraphs.en: NAM: Yeah, and a lot of concerns about whether all of this is going to pay off. And data centers are critical to AI companies, so when you have a wave of Democrats being elected talking about things like creating moratoriums or slowing down the development of data centers, investors can freak out.
paragraphs.zh: NAM: 是的，很多人都担心这一切是否能够带来回报。数据中心对人工智能公司至关重要，所以当一波民主党人当选并讨论诸如制定暂停令或减缓数据中心发展之类的事情时，投资者可能会感到恐慌。

paragraphs.en: KELLY: John, dig into that, if you would. Explain the freakout.
paragraphs.zh: 凯利：约翰，如果你愿意的话，深入研究一下。解释一下这种惊慌情绪。

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: Yeah. So there has been this boom in construction in AI data centers. There's trillions of dollars committed to more of them, but people are nervous about them - about the water and electricity costs, about what it means for jobs. I mean, just last night, I was at a town hall in San Jose, California. This is the heart of Silicon Valley, like, home turf for AI. And there are plans for as many as 13 new data centers there. Residents like Justin Brown say things are just moving way too fast.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：是的。所以在人工智能数据中心的建设方面出现了繁荣现象。已经有数万亿美元投入到更多的数据中心，但人们对它们感到紧张——担心水电成本，以及它对就业意味着什么。我的意思是，就在昨晚，我在加利福尼亚州圣何塞参加了一次市政厅会议。这里是硅谷的核心，算是人工智能的主阵地。而且计划在那里建多达13个新的数据中心。像贾斯廷·布朗这样的居民说，一切进展得太快了。

paragraphs.en: JUSTIN BROWN: Like, let's actually have a debate, and let's talk about this and see if there's some sort of common ground so the residents can get something out of this.
paragraphs.zh: 贾斯廷·布朗：比如，我们实际上来进行一场辩论，讨论一下这个问题，看看是否有某种共同点，这样居民们就能从中受益。

articles.title: Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank
articles.dek: In a new security bulletin, the information sharing and analysis center devoted to the healthcare industry, Health ISAC, alerted members to a recent wave of cyberattacks targeting refrigeration…

paragraphs.en: In a new security bulletin, the information sharing and analysis center devoted to the healthcare industry, Health ISAC, alerted members to a recent wave of cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers — including one incident that affected a major French blood bank.
paragraphs.zh: 在一份新的安全公告中，专注于医疗行业的信息共享与分析中心 Health ISAC 提醒其成员注意近期针对制冷控制器的一波网络攻击——其中一起事件影响了法国一家主要的血液银行。

paragraphs.en: "This alert is issued for situational awareness, highlighting how recent operational technology (OT) attacks against specific refrigeration brands directly intersect with emerging threats to the health sector," reads the bulletin seen by NPR. Operational technology refers to the machines that control physical processes in the real world, from cooling systems to water pumps.
paragraphs.zh: NPR看到的公告上写道：“此警报的发布是为了增强情境意识，强调近期针对特定制冷品牌的操作技术（OT）攻击如何与新兴的卫生部门威胁直接交叉。”操作技术是指控制现实世界物理过程的机器，从冷却系统到水泵。

paragraphs.en: Cyberattacks on grocery stores and food processing plants everywhere from Europe and Israel to U.S. military bases have drawn headlines in recent months, particularly as attacks have resulted in spoiled food, fires, broken machinery, and major business disruptions. Attackers are clearly aware of the vulnerability of these systems and are taking advantage.
paragraphs.zh: 针对从欧洲和以色列到美国军事基地的杂货店和食品加工厂的网络攻击在最近几个月引起了头条关注，特别是因为这些攻击导致了食物变质、火灾、设备损坏以及重大业务中断。攻击者显然意识到这些系统的脆弱性，并正在加以利用。

paragraphs.en: However, until news broke that the French blood bank, known as the French Blood Establishment, had also been targeted, there was less public attention focused on the potential consequences of refrigeration controllers failing in other industries, particularly healthcare, where lifesaving implements like blood and vaccines often require finely tuned temperature-controlled environments to remain viable.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，直到有消息传出法国血液银行，即法国血液机构，也成为目标之前，公众对制冷控制器在其他行业中失效可能带来的后果关注较少，尤其是在医疗行业，因为像血液和疫苗这样的救命工具通常需要精确调控的温控环境才能保持有效。

paragraphs.en: "This incident underscores a stark operational reality: cybersecurity in healthcare is fundamentally about patient safety," wrote Errol Weiss, the chief security officer at Health ISAC in an email to NPR. "When threat actors manipulate operational technology like cold-chain storage and refrigeration units holding donor blood, plasma, or critical therapies, they aren't merely stealing data or locking down administrative files, they are directly endangering the physical resources required to sustain human life."
paragraphs.zh: Health ISAC 的首席安全官 Errol Weiss 在给 NPR 的一封电子邮件中写道：“这一事件凸显了一个严峻的运营现实：医疗保健中的网络安全本质上关乎患者安全。当威胁行为者操纵如冷链储存和存放捐赠血液、血浆或关键治疗药物的制冷设备等运营技术时，他们不仅仅是在窃取数据或锁定管理文件，而是直接危及维持人类生命所需的物理资源。”

paragraphs.en: On Thursday, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the FBI, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the U.S. Department of Agriculture published their own fact sheet about threats to industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems, tools they identify as critical to multiple industries from healthcare to chemical production, food and agriculture, and transportation.
paragraphs.zh: 星期四，网络安全和基础设施安全局、联邦调查局、卫生与公共服务部以及美国农业部发布了关于工业制冷和冷链监控系统威胁的各自事实说明，这些工具被认为对从医疗保健到化学生产、食品与农业以及运输等多个行业至关重要。

paragraphs.en: The FBI Cyber Branch Operations director, Brett Leatherman, said the bureau is tracking bad actors targeting these systems "across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk."
paragraphs.zh: 联邦调查局网络分支机构运营主管布雷特·莱瑟曼表示，该局正在追踪针对这些系统的恶意行为者，“这些行为者遍及全球关键基础设施部门，使库存和设备面临风险。”

paragraphs.en: "Industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems protect food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive products, making them attractive targets for malicious cyber actors," Leatherman said.
paragraphs.zh: Leatherman 说：“工业制冷和冷链监控系统保护食品、药品及其他对温度敏感的产品，使它们成为恶意网络行为者的有吸引力的目标。”

articles.title: Even birds get jet lagged, study shows
articles.dek: New research shows that humans are not the only species to get jet lag: Some birds appear to experience it too.

paragraphs.en: New research shows that humans are not the only species to get jet lag: Some birds appear to experience it too.
paragraphs.zh: 新的研究表明，人类并不是唯一会经历时差反应的物种：一些鸟类似乎也会经历时差反应。

paragraphs.en: A study published in the journal Science found that a type of seabird known as the Manx shearwater appears to become slightly disoriented during long flights across the Atlantic Ocean. That disorientation, the authors say, is due to the bird's internal clock falling out of sync with the sun's position in the sky.
paragraphs.zh: 发表在《科学》杂志上的一项研究发现，一种被称为曼克斯剪尾海燕的海鸟在横穿大西洋的长途飞行中似乎会出现轻微的迷失方向。作者表示，这种迷失方向是由于鸟类的内部时钟与太阳在天空中的位置不同步所导致的。

paragraphs.en: Manx shearwaters are a common bird in the British Isles. They look a little like seagulls, but "they're actually very closely related to an albatross," said Patrick Lewin, a behavioral ecologist at the University of Oxford.
paragraphs.zh: 曼岛海燕是英伦群岛常见的鸟类。它们看起来有点像海鸥，但“它们实际上与信天翁关系非常密切，”牛津大学行为生态学家帕特里克·卢因说。

paragraphs.en: Shearwaters mate for life, and when they breed, a couple lays just one egg.
paragraphs.zh: 海燕终生配偶，当它们繁殖时，一对只会产一枚蛋。

paragraphs.en: Then they take turns incubating it: "One partner will sit on the egg nonstop while the other one goes out to sea," Lewin said.
paragraphs.zh: 然后它们轮流孵蛋：“一只伴侣会一直坐在蛋上，而另一只则出海，”卢因说道。

paragraphs.en: For up to two weeks the hunting partners scour the North Atlantic for fish and squid, often travelling hundreds of miles from their nests.
paragraphs.zh: 在长达两周的时间里，捕猎伙伴在北大西洋寻找鱼类和鱿鱼，常常从它们的巢穴出发，行程达数百英里。

paragraphs.en: Once these birds' bellies are full "they absolutely bomb it back to their colony," Lewin said. Often they make the long journey home in just a day or so.
paragraphs.zh: Lewin 说，一旦这些鸟的肚子吃饱了，“它们就会立即飞回自己的巢穴。” 它们通常只需一天左右的时间就能完成漫长的回家旅程。

paragraphs.en: Which raised an interesting question: Do Manx shearwaters feel jet lag (or perhaps more aptly, flap lag)?
paragraphs.zh: 这就引出了一个有趣的问题：马恩岛剪尾海燕会感到时差（或者更恰当地说，是拍翅时差）吗？

paragraphs.en: To see if these little birds really did feel the effects of flying through time zones like humans do, Lewin used a remarkable tool – for 20 years, his colleagues had been tagging birds with GPS trackers and collecting data on their flights out to the Atlantic and back.
paragraphs.zh: 为了看看这些小鸟是否真的像人类一样感受到穿越时区飞行的影响，卢因使用了一个非凡的工具——20年来，他的同事们一直在用GPS追踪器标记鸟类，并收集它们飞往大西洋及返回的飞行数据。

articles.title: Busy Philipps talks about treating her brain tumor and filming a new show
articles.dek: On Wild Card, Philipps unpacks the experience of treating her brain tumor and filming her new show, the CBS drama Cupertino. But she also opened up about another aspect of her life.

paragraphs.en: On Wild Card, Philipps unpacks the experience of treating her brain tumor and filming her new show, the CBS drama Cupertino. But she also opened up about another aspect of her life.
paragraphs.zh: 在《Wild Card》中，Philipps 讲述了她治疗脑瘤和拍摄新剧集 CBS 剧集《Cupertino》的经历。但她也谈到了自己生活中的另一个方面。

paragraphs.en: Each week, a guest draws a card from NPR's Wild Card deck and answers a big question about their life. Earlier this year, Busy Philipps had a morning that can give you whiplash. She had recently auditioned for the new CBS drama "Cupertino." And then she got two calls.
paragraphs.zh: 每周，一位嘉宾会从NPR的《Wild Card》牌堆中抽一张牌，并回答关于他们生活中的一个重大问题。今年早些时候，Busy Philipps经历了一个可能让你目不暇接的早晨。她最近为CBS的新剧《Cupertino》参加了试镜。然后她收到了两个电话。

paragraphs.en: BUSY PHILIPPS: I found out in the morning that "Cupertino" was happening. They were all so excited about me joining the cast. And a few hours later, Dr. Davinski called me from NYU and was like, you have a real brain tumor, and it's got to come out of your head. And I was like, OK, but I'm starting a new TV show (laughter), so I don't know if this is going to work for me.
paragraphs.zh: 比茜·菲利普斯：我早上才知道《库比蒂诺》要开拍。他们都对我加入剧组感到非常兴奋。几小时后，达文斯基医生从纽约大学给我打电话，说，你真的有一个脑瘤，必须从你脑子里取出来。我当时的反应是，好吧，但我正准备开一档新的电视剧（笑声），所以我不知道这是否适合我。

paragraphs.en: KELLY: On Wild Card, Philipps unpacks the experience of treating her brain tumor and filming that new show. She also opened up about another aspect of her life with host Rachel Martin, and we will note, this conversation does touch on sex and child sexual assault.
paragraphs.zh: 凯利：在《Wild Card》中，菲利普斯讲述了她治疗脑瘤和拍摄新节目的经历。她还向主持人瑞秋·马丁敞开心扉，谈到了她生活的另一个方面，我们需要说明的是，这段对话确实涉及性和儿童性侵话题。

paragraphs.en: RACHEL MARTIN: What's something you love that you discovered later in life?
paragraphs.zh: 瑞秋·马丁：你晚年才发现但却很喜欢的东西是什么？

paragraphs.en: PHILIPPS: No, I mean, I had sex very early, but I think I was, like, not - I think I had been raped, and I was a woman of a - and I'm a woman of a certain age.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯：不，我是说，我很早就发生了性关系，但我想，我不是——我想我曾经被强奸过，而且我是一个——我是一个有一定年纪的女性。

paragraphs.en: PHILIPPS: ...Just was brought up in an era where, like, our pleasure was not a thing that we were sort of encouraged to even explore.
paragraphs.zh: PHILIPPS: ……只是生长在那个时代，我们的快乐几乎不是一种我们被鼓励去探索的东西。

paragraphs.en: PHILIPPS: And I didn't really - I, like, didn't get it kind of in a weird way.
paragraphs.zh: PHILIPPS：其实我也没有完全明白——有点奇怪，我就是没弄懂。

articles.title: Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
articles.dek: ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay — Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday after the collapse of a major digital bank tied to his government triggered widespread protests, froze…

paragraphs.en: ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay — Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday after the collapse of a major digital bank tied to his government triggered widespread protests, froze millions of people's savings and cost him the support of his own party.
paragraphs.zh: 巴拉圭亚松森——巴拉圭总统圣地亚哥·佩尼亚在周四宣布辞职，此前与他政府有关的一家大型数字银行倒闭，引发了大规模抗议，冻结了数百万人的储蓄，并使他失去了自己党派的支持。

paragraphs.en: The crisis at Ueno Bank turned Peña's long-ruling Colorado Party against him, a stunning reversal for the former International Monetary Fund economist who had enjoyed the backing of the country's most powerful politicians and was welcomed in Washington just weeks ago as a key ally of the Trump administration.
paragraphs.zh: 上野银行的危机使佩尼亚长期执政的科罗拉多党转而反对他，这对这位曾享有国内最有权势政治家支持，并在几周前被华盛顿欢迎为特朗普政府关键盟友的前国际货币基金组织经济学家来说，是一次令人震惊的逆转。

paragraphs.en: Minutes after Peña's announcement, the lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, sending the charges to the Senate. Congressional leaders were expected to accept his resignation later Thursday, clearing the way for Vice President Pedro Alliana to be sworn in without waiting for a Senate trial.
paragraphs.zh: 在佩尼亚宣布后几分钟，下议院以78票对0票投票弹劾他，并将指控送交参议院。预计国会领导人将在周四晚些时候接受他的辞职，为副总统佩德罗·阿利亚纳在无需等待参议院审判的情况下宣誓就职铺平道路。

paragraphs.en: Opposition senators were still demanding a trial, arguing that allowing Peña to resign would preserve his eligibility to become a senator for life, with legal protections that could prevent his prosecution.
paragraphs.zh: 反对派参议员仍然要求审判，他们认为允许佩尼亚辞职将保留他成为终身参议员的资格，并享有可能阻止他被起诉的法律保护。

paragraphs.en: As lawmakers debated his impeachment, Peña said in a video posted to X that he was stepping down in the interest of "the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions."
paragraphs.zh: 当立法者讨论对他进行弹劾时，佩尼亚在发布到 X 的视频中表示，他是为了“国家的稳定、社会和平以及维护我们民主制度的需要”而辞职。

paragraphs.en: Even Peña's mentor, Colorado Party leader and former President Horacio Cartes, backed impeachment, saying the party would not side with "the plundering of public and private funds and pensioners' money." The United States Treasury sanctioned Cartes in 2023 over bribery allegations that the Trump administration lifted last year.
paragraphs.zh: 甚至佩尼亚的导师、科罗拉多党领导人及前总统霍拉西奥·卡尔特斯也支持弹劾，他表示该党不会支持“对公共和私人资金以及养老金资金的掠夺”。由于贿赂指控，美国财政部在2023年对卡尔特斯实施了制裁，而特朗普政府去年取消了这些制裁。

paragraphs.en: Peña, who until last year held a stake in a company linked to Ueno, expressed contrition. But he stopped short of accepting responsibility for the turmoil, which has left millions of depositors, retirees and workers scrambling to recoup their frozen savings and unpaid wages.
paragraphs.zh: 佩尼亚直到去年还持有与上野有关的公司股份，他表示了悔意。但他没有完全承担造成混乱的责任，这场混乱让数百万储户、退休人员和工人争相追回被冻结的储蓄和未支付的工资。

paragraphs.en: "I want to apologize to the people if I have failed them at any point," he said. "It was never my intention to betray the trust they placed in me."
paragraphs.zh: “如果我在任何时候辜负了人民，我想向他们道歉，”他说。“我从未打算背叛他们对我的信任。”

articles.title: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
articles.dek: Two days after Democrats won overwhelmingly in the national midterm elections — and in state races across the country — investors started to come to terms with the potential consequences.

paragraphs.en: Two days after Democrats won overwhelmingly in the national midterm elections — and in state races across the country — investors started to come to terms with the potential consequences.
paragraphs.zh: 在全国中期选举以及全国各州的选举中，民主党大获全胜两天后，投资者开始意识到潜在的后果。

paragraphs.en: Fears that an incoming Democratic Congress would crack down on AI sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq down more than 5% and wiped out more than $2 trillion in market value. The Dow Jones and S&P also sank.
paragraphs.zh: 对即将到来的民主党主导的国会将打压人工智能的担忧，使以科技股为主的纳斯达克下跌超过5%，市值蒸发超过2万亿美元。道琼斯和标准普尔指数也下跌了。

paragraphs.en: The losses were a stark reversal from Wednesday, when investors had initially sent shares higher across the board, relieved that the midterms did not end with the fate of Congress undecided.
paragraphs.zh: 这些损失与周三形成了鲜明对比，当时投资者最初将股票普遍推高，因为他们松了一口气，认为中期选举没有以国会命运未定而结束。

paragraphs.en: The sobering-up seen across markets on Thursday reflected investors' concern about a big signal sent by voters: They revolted against AI data centers, which many people worry will gobble up water and energy resources. Those voters supported Democrats who have vowed to push back against the proliferation of these projects.
paragraphs.zh: 周四市场的冷静反应反映了投资者对选民发出的重大信号的担忧：选民反对人工智能数据中心，许多人担心这些数据中心会消耗大量水和能源资源。这些选民支持那些承诺抵制这些项目扩张的民主党人。

paragraphs.en: But many AI companies — including Meta and Alphabet, the parent company of Google — need to keep building out these data centers to continue developing the technology.
paragraphs.zh: 但是许多人工智能公司——包括Meta和谷歌的母公司Alphabet——需要继续建设这些数据中心，以继续开发这项技术。

paragraphs.en: The Nasdaq's decline comes after what has already been a rough year of technology shares on Wall Street, with investors starting to question whether the massive investments companies have plowed into AI will pay off anytime soon.
paragraphs.zh: 纳斯达克的下跌是在科技股已经经历了艰难的一年的背景下发生的，投资者开始质疑公司投向人工智能的大量投资是否会在短期内带来回报。

paragraphs.en: "There is some concern regarding AI regulation, and fears that there could be far more regulations coming to AI technology, as well as a pushback on the buildout of data centers across the country," says David Busch, chief investment officer of Trajan Wealth.
paragraphs.zh: Trajan Wealth 的首席投资官 David Busch 表示：“人们对人工智能的监管存在一些担忧，并且担心可能会出台更多针对人工智能技术的监管，同时全国范围内数据中心的建设也可能受到阻力。”

paragraphs.en: AI-related or AI-dependent stocks of all kinds were among the biggest decliners on Thursday, with Tesla and SpaceX — both controlled by billionaire Elon Musk — falling particularly sharply. Musk spent hundreds of millions of dollars in an unsuccessful attempt to elect more Republicans, and investors fear he and his companies could also come under Democratic scrutiny when the new Congress is seated in January.
paragraphs.zh: 各种与人工智能相关或依赖人工智能的股票在周四是跌幅最大的，其中特斯拉和太空探索公司——两者都由亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克控制——跌幅尤为明显。马斯克花费了数亿美元试图让更多共和党人当选，但未能成功，投资者担心他和他的公司在新一届国会于一月就职后，也可能受到民主党的审查。

articles.title: Review: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is superb, streamlined and safe
articles.dek: With its tale of an idyllic world despoiled by the lust for power, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels as relevant today as it did in 1998. Nintendo's new remake, out Thursday on the Switch…

paragraphs.en: With its tale of an idyllic world despoiled by the lust for power, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels as relevant today as it did in 1998. Nintendo's new remake, out Thursday on the Switch 2, enshrines its place in the gaming canon for generations to come. But despite its stupendous production values and painstaking details, the game left me feeling oddly bereft.
paragraphs.zh: 凭借关于一个因权力欲望而被破坏的田园世界的故事，《塞尔达传说：时之笛》在今天仍然和1998年一样具有现实意义。任天堂的新重制版将于周四在Switch 2上发布，确保其在游戏经典中的地位能够传承几代人。但尽管其制作价值惊人，细节精雕细琢，这款游戏仍让我感到莫名的空虚。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps I should have expected as much. Ocarina of Time weaponizes nostalgia even within its narrative, as the protagonist Link ventures to save his post-apocalyptic world as an adult after first working through it as a kid. You'll uncover old characters enduring new catastrophes. You'll try to rescue everyone you meet. You'll strive to bring things back to how they were before — no, better than they were before.
paragraphs.zh: 也许我早该料到如此。《时之笛》即使在其叙事中也利用了怀旧感，当主角林克在孩童时期经历过这个世界后，再作为成年人去拯救他那后末日的世界。你会遇到老角色经历新的灾难。你会尝试拯救你遇到的每一个人。你会努力让一切恢复到以前的样子——不，恢复得比以前更好。

paragraphs.en: Seven years stretch between Link's childhood and adult adventures. 28 years yawn between the remake and the original's release. Both in and out of the game, Ocarina of Time makes us yearn for an idealized past.
paragraphs.zh: 林克的童年与成年冒险之间相隔七年。《时之笛》重制版与原版发布之间相隔二十八年。无论在游戏内外，《时之笛》都让我们渴望一个理想化的过去。

paragraphs.en: Decent remakes evoke how you remember a game rather than re-create dated controls and chunky graphics. In myriad small ways, Nintendo has brought Ocarina of Time up to contemporary standards while (mostly) preserving its soul.
paragraphs.zh: 体面的重制版唤起你对游戏的记忆，而不是重新创建过时的操作和粗糙的画面。在无数细微之处，任天堂已经将《时之笛》提升到现代标准，同时（大部分）保留了其灵魂。

paragraphs.en: I miss the thoughtfully-composed camera angles from the original, but quickly got used to the over-the-shoulder camera the remake employs (though I was irked that it abandoned the top-down view when you sneak into Hyrule Castle). The new jump and sprint buttons made navigating the world feel more natural. Combat's smoother too, though it's still not easy to switch between targeted enemies (unlike modern third-person games like Elden Ring, where you can toggle between foes by simply flicking the right stick).
paragraphs.zh: 我怀念原作中精心设计的摄像机角度，但很快就习惯了重制版使用的肩膀视角摄像机（尽管当我潜入海利亚城时，它放弃了俯视视角让我感到恼火）。新的跳跃和冲刺按钮让探索世界的感觉更自然。战斗也更流畅了，尽管在切换目标敌人时仍然不容易（不像现代第三人称游戏《艾尔登法环》，你只需轻弹右摇杆就能在敌人之间切换）。

paragraphs.en: You can, thankfully, swap between items in a quick menu — the same system introduced to the series in 2023's Tears of the Kingdom and continued in 2024's Echoes of Wisdom. It's still not as fast as I'd wish (I'd have preferred a customizable wheel), but I vastly prefer it to constantly pausing to access my equipment. It made it easy to change my strategy on the fly. I'd often cast Naryu's Love and deploy Bombchus, for example, where before I'd mostly stick to the Longshot and Bow.
paragraphs.zh: 值得庆幸的是，你可以在快速菜单中切换物品——这是在2023年的《王国之泪》中首次引入该系列的系统，并在2024年的《智慧回声》中继续使用。它仍然没有我期望的那么快（我更希望有一个可自定义的轮盘），但我仍远远更喜欢它，而不是不断暂停来访问我的装备。这让即时改变策略变得很容易。例如，我经常会施放纳吕之爱并布置炸弹鼠，而以前我大多只使用长钩和弓。

paragraphs.en: If you get stuck, a new "Threads of Time" quest log can point you in the right direction (though you'll likely still need to look up a guide for the convoluted Biggoron Sword quest!). And yes, the notoriously frustrating Water Temple is much more tolerable this time around. But mind your rupees! Inflation's hit Hyrule. While wallets can now carry double the cash that they used to, Great Fairy upgrades are no longer free. They can cost up to 500 rupees!
paragraphs.zh: 如果你卡住了，全新的“时间之线”任务日志可以为你指明正确的方向（尽管你可能仍然需要查阅指南来完成复杂的比格隆之剑任务！）。是的，臭名昭著的令人沮丧的水之神庙这次要容易得多。但注意你的卢比！通货膨胀已经影响了海利亚。虽然钱包现在可以携带双倍的现金，但大精灵升级不再免费，可能需要高达500卢比！

paragraphs.en: It's the remake's aesthetic changes that stand out most. The game's astonishingly ornate textures can jar with its cartoony proportions. Ninety-eight percent of the time the translation is a clear upgrade, but other times it leads straight into the uncanny valley (Nabooru looks bizarrely yassified with huge red lips and golden eye-shadow, for example).
paragraphs.zh: 最引人注目的是重制版的美学变化。游戏异常华丽的纹理可能会与其卡通化的比例产生冲突。百分之九十八的情况下，这次翻译明显是一次提升，但有时却直接进入了恐怖谷（例如，纳布鲁看起来奇怪地被美化了，有着巨大的红唇和金色眼影）。

articles.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
articles.dek: The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府正在提议大幅缩减拜登时代的一项规则，该规则旨在减少全国范围内钻探现场石油和天然气行业的甲烷排放。

paragraphs.en: Methane is a major contributor to climate change and is estimated to be 80 times more planet-warming than carbon dioxide in a twenty-year time frame. In 2023, the Biden administration finalized rules that were meant to rein in methane emissions from the oil and gas sector.
paragraphs.zh: 甲烷是导致气候变化的主要因素，据估计，在二十年的时间范围内，其对地球变暖的影响是二氧化碳的80倍。2023年，拜登政府最终制定了旨在限制石油和天然气行业甲烷排放的规则。

paragraphs.en: President Trump made the announcement while campaigning in Lubbock, Texas, Tuesday, saying his administration's revision, under the Clean Air Act, would save the industry billions in production costs and spur more domestic drilling. The proposal comes as Republicans face a backlash from voters over high gas prices heading into the midterms.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统周二在德克萨斯州拉伯克竞选时宣布此事，称其政府根据《清洁空气法》修订将为行业节省数十亿美元的生产成本，并促进更多国内钻探。该提案出台之际，共和党面临选民对高昂天然气价格的强烈反弹，临近中期选举。

paragraphs.en: "Behind every barrel of oil and every cubic foot of natural gas produced in the U.S. are millions of workers, businesses, and the heartbeat of this nation's economy. The Biden EPA destructively targeted all this," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a press release.
paragraphs.zh: 美国环保局局长李·泽尔丁在一份新闻稿中表示：“在美国生产的每一桶石油和每一立方英尺的天然气背后，都有数百万工人、企业以及这个国家经济的脉搏。拜登政府的环保局以破坏性的方式针对了这一切。”

paragraphs.en: The oil and gas industry, which vigorously opposed the 2023 rules, said EPA's proposed rollback will address some of the challenges companies have faced in trying to comply with the regulations.
paragraphs.zh: 积极反对2023年规则的石油和天然气行业表示，环保局提议的撤销将解决公司在尝试遵守这些法规时面临的部分挑战。

paragraphs.en: "We look forward to working with the Trump administration on a more workable approach that supports American energy production, provides greater regulatory certainty and advances continued emissions reductions," Dustin Meyer, vice president at the American Petroleum Institute, a trade organization for the U.S. oil and gas industry, said in a statement.
paragraphs.zh: 美国石油协会（一家美国石油和天然气行业的贸易组织）副总裁达斯汀·迈耶在一份声明中表示：“我们期待与特朗普政府合作，采取一种更可行的方法，支持美国能源生产，提供更大的监管确定性，并推进持续的减排。”

paragraphs.en: But environmentalists say this may end up actually costing the industry more.
paragraphs.zh: 但环保人士表示，这实际上可能会让行业花费更多。

paragraphs.en: "Methane is natural gas, or natural gas is methane," says Jon Goldstein, associate vice president at the Environmental Defense Fund. "And so if you're capturing more natural gas, you're not allowing it to leak out, you're not allowing it to be flared, you have more product that you can sell. And so that offsets a lot of the costs."
paragraphs.zh: 环境保护基金副总裁乔恩·戈德斯坦说：“甲烷就是天然气，或者说天然气就是甲烷。如果你捕获了更多的天然气，就不会让它泄漏，也不会让它被燃烧掉，你就有更多的产品可以出售。这就抵消了很多成本。”

articles.title: A judge blocks construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval
articles.dek: A federal judge blocked construction of President Trump's arch early Friday morning, stopping work the administration had hoped to begin immediately.

paragraphs.en: A federal judge blocked construction of President Trump's arch early Friday morning, stopping work the administration had hoped to begin immediately.
paragraphs.zh: 周五清晨，一名联邦法官阻止了特朗普总统拱门的建设，停止了政府原本希望立即开始的工作。

paragraphs.en: Just before midnight, District Court Judge Tanya Chutkan issued an order barring the government from any construction work for 14 days, granting a request filed days earlier by the governments of D.C. and Virginia.
paragraphs.zh: 就在午夜前，地区法院法官Tanya Chutkan发布了一项命令，禁止政府进行任何建设工作，为期14天，这项命令是应华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州政府几天前提出的请求而批准的。

paragraphs.en: She laid out her reasoning in a 33-page opinion, in which she scrutinized the administration's competing justifications for the arch — particularly its sudden emphasis on national security — and agreed that the local governments are likely to be harmed by its construction. The 250-foot arch would stand in Memorial Circle, a traffic island on the bridge linking the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery.
paragraphs.zh: 她在一份33页的意见书中阐述了她的推理，其中她仔细审查了政府对拱门提出的相互矛盾的理由——特别是其对国家安全突如其来的强调——并同意地方政府可能会因其建设而受到损害。这个250英尺高的拱门将矗立在纪念圆环上，该圆环是连接林肯纪念堂和阿灵顿国家公墓的大桥上的一个交通岛。

paragraphs.en: Trump administration officials have said work would take place 20 hours a day, year-round, for two to three years. In addition to questioning the arch's legality, D.C. and Virginia argue the construction would cause all sorts of financial and logistical disruptions.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府官员表示，这项工作将全年每天进行 20 小时，持续两到三年。除了质疑拱门的合法性，华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州还认为建设将引起各种财务和后勤方面的干扰。

paragraphs.en: "The threatened harms will materialize as soon as construction begins, in part because the traffic disruptions will occur immediately," Chutkan agreed.
paragraphs.zh: Chutkan同意，“一旦施工开始，威胁的损害将立即显现，部分原因是交通中断将立即发生。”

paragraphs.en: Chutkan's ruling came less than two hours after a federal planning commission packed with presidential allies granted final approval to the arch in an 8-4 vote. The National Capital Planning Commission heard nearly eight hours of impassioned pleas from veterans, lawmakers, residents and concerned citizens opposed to the structure.
paragraphs.zh: Chutkan的裁决是在一个由总统盟友组成的联邦规划委员会以8比4投票最终批准拱门不到两小时后做出的。国家首都规划委员会听取了退伍军人、立法者、居民和反对该建筑的关切公民近八小时充满激情的呼吁。

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration had previously told the court it could begin excavation work that same day, despite lacking authorization from Congress and an expanding legal challenge.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府此前曾告诉法庭，尽管缺乏国会授权并面临日益扩大的法律挑战，但它可以在同一天开始挖掘工作。

paragraphs.en: A group of Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian sued the government earlier this year, arguing that an arch is unlawful without Congressional approval, which the administration has not sought. The Democratic governments of D.C. and Virginia jointly filed a similar lawsuit last weekend.
paragraphs.zh: 今年早些时候，一群越战老兵和一位建筑历史学家起诉了政府，认为拱门如果没有国会批准是违法的，而政府并未寻求该批准。上周末，华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州的民主党政府联合提起了类似的诉讼。
